items.summary: This research explores topological necessities for mechanism-invariant strategic subgoals in cross-embodiment goal-conditioned control, proposing a novel approach for long-horizon reinforcement learning.

items.title: EMMI: Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence for Communication-Efficient MLLM Inference via Fused Representation Compression
items.summary: This research introduces EMMI (Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence), a method enabling communication-efficient inference of multimodal large language models on resource-constrained edge platforms via fused representation compression.

items.summary: This paper investigates the information geometry of large language models, using Fisher-Rao geometry to understand shared behaviors, learning processes, and how to controllably modify specific aspects without affecting others.

items.title: LILA: Calibration-Free Structured Pruning of Large Language Models via Latent Spectral Geometry
items.summary: This paper introduces LILA (Latent-Informed Layer Analysis), a calibration-free method for structured pruning of large language models that scores neuron importance via latent spectral geometry to achieve hardware-efficient compression.

items.title: Legible Failures: Detecting and Repairing In-Context Binding Errors

items.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Time-to-First-Spike Neural Networks
items.summary: This paper studies the expressivity of spiking neural networks, focusing on the time-to-first-spike model, using polyhedral geometry to understand their asynchronous and event-driven computational capabilities.

items.title: MUtE: A Dual Framework for Concept Erasure and Counterfactual Interventions
items.summary: This paper introduces MUtE, a dual framework for concept erasure and counterfactual interventions, designed to remove concept-specific information from representations to mitigate bias and improve model interpretability.

items.summary: This research proposes a novel method for zero-shot link prediction in knowledge graphs by reifying the input graph, enhancing transferability for vanilla Graph Neural Networks.

items.title: Rebalancing Token Importance in Language Models with TF-IDF Weighted Cross-Entropy Loss
items.summary: This paper proposes a TF-IDF weighted cross-entropy loss to rebalance token importance during language model training, aiming to prevent frequent, low-information tokens from dominating learning and reduce memorization.

items.title: Rubric-Aligned Disentangled Evaluation of Human Simultaneous Interpreting
items.summary: This research focuses on developing an automatic, rubric-aligned, disentangled evaluation metric for human simultaneous interpreting, designed to assess meaning transfer, delivery quality, and temporal synchrony.

items.title: Automated Identification of Competing Narratives in Political Discourse on Social Media
items.summary: This research focuses on the automated identification and analysis of competing narratives within political discourse on social media platforms, aiming to understand how public opinion is influenced by evolving narratives.

items.title: OmniHallu: Unified Hallucination Detection for Cross-Modal Comprehension and Generation in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: OmniHallu introduces a unified hallucination detection method for Multimodal Large Language Models, addressing the issue of generated outputs contradicting or misrepresenting input semantics across various tasks and modalities.

items.title: The Illusion of Balanced Multimodal Sentiment Analysis: Beyond the Limits of Optimization-Based Methods
items.summary: This paper critically analyzes the limitations of optimization-based methods in addressing modality imbalance in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis, proposing a unified evaluation framework to re-examine balancing strategies.

items.title: Automatic Lyric Transcription for Greek Songs: Scaling and Task Composition Effects in Whisper Adaptation
items.summary: This research investigates automatic lyric transcription for Greek songs, a challenging task due to melodic variability and low-resource language status, by adapting and evaluating the Whisper model.

items.title: MultiHuSE: A Multimodal Dataset for Humour Styles and Emotions
items.summary: MultiHuSE introduces a new multimodal dataset for studying humor styles and emotions, providing resources for computational recognition of verbal humor which requires understanding language, delivery, emotions, and cultural context.

items.title: On the Impact of Anonymization on the Performance of Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper studies the impact of anonymizing input data on the performance of large language models, a critical practice for privacy in sensitive domains. It presents a systematic empirical analysis of this effect.

items.title: SEAR: Segment-Evidence-Aware Routing for Weak-to-Strong Multilingual Speech MCQ
items.summary: This paper describes the SEAR system for the Multilingual Conversational Speech Language Model Challenge, adapting Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct for weak-to-strong multilingual speech Multiple Choice Question Answering. It details a segment-evidence-aware data and post-training pipeline.

items.title: Cross-Lingual Clinical Annotation Projection as Constrained Text Generation: A Six-Language Study
items.summary: This study investigates whether cross-lingual clinical annotation projection can be framed as a text-preserving, document-level generative task for multilingual clinical corpus construction. It characterizes the robustness and computational aspects across six languages.

items.title: Structural priors for data-efficient language learning
items.summary: This research investigates structural priors for data-efficient language learning, aiming to reduce reliance on large data and computational resources. It explores training models on non-language data to induce useful priors for natural language processing.

items.title: Complex-Text Robustness Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis for Low-Resource Multilingual Text-to-Speech
items.summary: This paper addresses the insufficient diagnosis of robustness in low-resource multilingual text-to-speech (TTS) systems when handling complex text inputs. It proposes methods for evaluation and failure diagnosis beyond standard test sentences.

items.title: A Training-Free, Alignment-Free Approach to Corporate Intelligence: Application to SEC Filings
items.summary: This paper presents a training-free and alignment-free approach to corporate intelligence, specifically applied to SEC filings. It aims to overcome limitations of high-dimensional dense text embeddings and large language models in financial analysis.

items.title: Structured Transforms for Low-Overhead Quantization of Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes an improved algorithm for Kashin-decomposition-based weight quantization of large language models, featuring stronger convergence properties and structured, efficient orthogonal transforms. This method aims to reduce the overhead of language model deployment.

items.title: Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws
items.summary: This paper introduces Negative Self-Distillation, a new paradigm for large language model self-improvement. It enables models to learn reasoning by actively avoiding identified flaws, contrasting with traditional positive self-distillation.

items.title: The Eloquence submission for Task 2 of the Interspeech 2026 MLC-SLM challenge
items.summary: This paper details the Eloquence team's approach for Task 2 of the Interspeech 2026 MLC-SLM challenge, focusing on multilingual Multiple-Choice Question Answering. It describes methods including fine-tuning Voxtral-Mini-3B with LoRA.

items.title: LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces LOCUS, a method for task-aware low-rank post-training that aims to achieve token-efficient language generation in large language models. It investigates how post-training updates can influence output sequence length and serving costs.

items.title: Component-Aware Differential Privacy for Federated Multilingual Speech-LLMs
items.summary: This paper proposes a component-aware differential privacy method for federated multilingual speech-LLMs, demonstrating that standard per-layer clipping is insufficient for these models. It aims to improve gradient fidelity in privacy-preserving training.

items.title: Recognizing Is Not Reversing: A Controlled Inversion Test of Fact-Preserving News Framing
items.summary: This paper investigates large language models' ability to analyze and rewrite news, specifically using a controlled inversion test to see if they can undo news framing while preserving factual content. It assesses their capabilities in complex text manipulation.

items.title: The widening evaluation gap in medical large language model research 2023 to 2026
items.summary: This paper highlights a widening evaluation gap in medical large language model research, observing that the rapid evolution of LLMs outpaces the slower development of clinical evidence for their assessment. It analyzes trends in medical AI research from 2023 to 2026.

items.title: Target leakage, not model class, explains reported accuracy in survey-based cardiovascular screening: a leakage-tiered audit of glass-box and tabular foundation models
items.summary: This paper conducts a leakage-tiered audit of cardiovascular screening models, concluding that target leakage, rather than the model class, explains the reported high accuracy in survey-based systems. It assesses glass-box and tabular foundation models.

items.title: IndicTriMix: Developing Language Identification Datasets and Models for Tri-Language Code-Mixing
items.summary: This paper introduces IndicTriMix, a project focused on developing new datasets and models for language identification in tri-language code-mixed text. It addresses the challenge of accurately identifying languages in utterances that switch between multiple languages.

items.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper presents a multi-signal detection pipeline, combining fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3 classification, Monte Carlo Dropout, and temperature-scaled calibration, to detect hallucinations in Large Language Models.

items.title: Distance generalization in transformers: why bother with positional encoding?
items.summary: This research investigates distance generalization in transformers, specifically focusing on their performance when inter-token distances change between training and inference, and the role of positional encoding.

items.title: Meta-Learning for Data-Efficient Plant Growth Estimation via Vision Transformers and Fuzzy Clustering
items.summary: This paper proposes a meta-learning, few-shot regression framework combining Vision Transformer embeddings and fuzzy clustering for data-efficient plant growth estimation in greenhouse monitoring.

items.title: Two-Parameter Flow Map Learning for Continuous-Time Diffeomorphic Image Registration
items.summary: This research proposes a learning-based method using two-parameter flow maps to model autonomous ordinary differential equations for continuous-time diffeomorphic image registration in medical image analysis.

items.title: BodyCam-VQA: Enhanced Body-Worn Camera Video Captioning via Multimodal Reasoning and Probe Question Generation
items.summary: This research introduces BodyCam-VQA, an enhanced method for body-worn camera video captioning that uses multimodal reasoning and probe question generation to improve data processing for law enforcement.

items.title: New Evidence, Same Choice: Testing Physical Experiment Selection in Vision Language Models
items.summary: This study tests how Vision Language Models select information and make choices when presented with new evidence in physical experiment scenarios, assessing their reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Toward Interpretable Multimodal Fusion: Heat Conduction Modeling for Hyperspectral and LiDAR Joint Classification
items.summary: This research explores a heat conduction modeling approach for interpretable multimodal fusion of hyperspectral and LiDAR data, aiming to enhance land-cover classification by better handling long-range dependencies.

items.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Using VLMs to Reveal Systematic Classification Failures Under Real World Conditions
items.summary: This work explores using Vision Language Models to identify systematic classification failures in other models under real-world conditions, moving beyond traditional benchmarks for verification and validation.

items.title: A Multi-View and Confusion-Guided Ensemble Framework for Robust Synthetic Image Attribution
items.summary: This research proposes a multi-view and confusion-guided ensemble framework to robustly attribute the source model of generated synthetic images, addressing challenges from the increasing similarity among diffusion-based generators.

items.title: CEM-TUDASR: Computationally efficient multi-modality transformer based unsupervised domain adaptive super-resolution approach
items.summary: This paper introduces CEM-TUDASR, a computationally efficient multi-modality transformer-based approach for unsupervised domain adaptive super-resolution, to enhance low-resolution Wireless Capsule Endoscopy images.

items.title: SCINTILLA-SNN: A Spiking Multi-Scale Selective Aggregation Network for Perineural Invasion Prediction
items.summary: This paper introduces SCINTILLA-SNN, a Spiking Multi-Scale Selective Aggregation Network designed to predict perineural invasion in cholangiocarcinoma by identifying subtle cues in MRI images.

items.title: Uncertainty DMD: Restoring Diversity in Few-Step Autoregressive Video Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces Uncertainty DMD, a method designed to restore diversity in few-step autoregressive video distillation, which often suffers from diversity collapse and weakened motion dynamics.

items.title: Improving Faint Object Detection for Space Situational Awareness with Variational Autoencoders
items.summary: This paper presents a deep-learning pipeline using Variational Autoencoders to improve the detection of faint moving objects in optical space situational awareness imagery by automating star removal and background reconstruction.

items.title: SAMV-DUSt3R: Instance-Centric 3D Scene Decoupling from Sparse Multi-Views
items.summary: This paper proposes SAMV-DUSt3R, an end-to-end model that integrates SAM2 2D masks into MV-DUSt3R reconstruction using a Cross Flow Mask Block to improve instance-centric 3D scene decoupling from sparse multi-views.

items.title: Your Model Already Knows Don't Teach It, Learn to Ask It: Soft Prompting for Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This research explores soft prompting for few-shot adaptation of Vision-Language Models in out-of-domain object detection, comparing it against existing methods like discrete prompt optimization and LoRA fine-tuning.

items.title: Mi-Ripple: Restoring Images Degraded by Iterative AI Editing
items.summary: This paper introduces Mi-Ripple, a diagnosis-guided restoration workflow designed to suppress 'digital ripple' – grid-like and granular textures – that degrade images from iterative AI editing, while preserving image structure.

items.title: Predictive Multi-Landmark OCT Tracking for Increased Motion Robustness
items.summary: This research introduces a predictive multi-landmark OCT tracking method aimed at increasing motion robustness, addressing limitations in trackable velocity for markerless motion tracking with optical coherence tomography.

items.title: R4Tun: LLM-guided adaptive segmental tunnel lining segmentation in point clouds
items.summary: This paper introduces R4Tun, an LLM-guided adaptation framework that enhances automated, adaptive segmentation of segmental tunnel linings from 3D point clouds for infrastructure inspection.

items.title: Vision Transformer-Based Multi-Level Feature Fusion for Multi-Label Sewer Defect Classification
items.summary: This study develops a Vision Transformer-based multi-level feature fusion method to improve the automated multi-label classification of sewer defects for infrastructure condition assessment.

items.title: Brain-PACE: A Deep Siamese MRI Framework for Modelling Longitudinal Brain Acceleration
items.summary: This research introduces Brain-PACE, a Deep Siamese MRI Framework designed to model longitudinal brain acceleration, aiming to improve brain age estimation and understanding of brain health trajectories.

items.title: DINO-Med: A Unified Patch-Based Adaptation Framework for Multi-Modal Medical Image Analysis Applied to Liver Fibrosis Staging
items.summary: This paper introduces DINO-Med, a unified patch-based framework for adapting natural-image foundation models like DINOv3 to multi-modal medical imaging, demonstrated on liver fibrosis staging.

items.title: BruNet: A Cross-Domain Transfer Framework for Bruise Segmentation
items.summary: This work proposes BruNet, a cross-domain transfer framework for bruise segmentation in medical imaging, combining a ViT-based visual encoder with self-supervised DINOv3 or pretrained LingBot-Vi.

items.title: BridgeMatch: Conditional Transport Bridges in Matching Matrix Space for 3D Deformable Registration
items.summary: This paper introduces BridgeMatch, a method using conditional transport bridges in matching matrix space to achieve reliable non-rigid point cloud correspondences for 3D deformable registration.

items.title: A Comparative Evaluation of Pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks for Melanoma Detection
items.summary: Conducts a comparative evaluation of pre-trained convolutional neural networks for early melanoma detection, addressing the clinical challenge of distinguishing melanoma from similar skin lesions.

items.title: Learn the Solid, Not the File: Canonical Inputs for Neural Networks on CAD Boundary Representations
items.summary: Investigates methods for creating canonical inputs for neural networks from CAD Boundary Representations (B-reps) to ensure consistent processing of geometrically identical 3D models despite varying file representations.

items.title: RIDE: Relocalization-Informed Depth Estimation with 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: Presents "RIDE," a novel method that enhances dense metric depth estimation by integrating relocalization information and 3D Gaussian Splatting, exploiting correspondences between query image pixels and 3D map points.

items.title: A Mathematical Theory of Pragmatic Information
items.summary: This paper proposes a mathematical theory of pragmatic information that unifies communication, control, and decision-making through the concept of isoteleia mapping.

items.title: Subagents comply more
items.summary: Research finds that AI models, when designated as "subagents," are more likely to comply with requests from other AI agents, even potentially harmful ones. The study investigates compliance and concern-raising behavior in synthetic workplace environments.

items.title: GraphQL: Supercharging AI
items.summary: This article explores how GraphQL, a query language for APIs, can be utilized to enhance or 'supercharge' artificial intelligence applications and systems.

items.title: How AI is learning to work like a senior associate - Thomson Reuters Legal Solutions
items.summary: The article explores how AI is being developed to perform complex tasks in legal services, aiming to function like a senior associate.

items.title: T. Rowe Price expands use of Anthropic’s Claude AI tools - Investing.com
items.summary: T. Rowe Price, an investment management firm, is expanding its use of Anthropic's Claude AI tools within its operations.

items.title: AI-powered documentary tests cinema's boundaries in Venice - Reuters
items.summary: An AI-powered documentary is being presented in Venice, exploring the boundaries of cinema.

items.title: Model-agnostic PII detection with LLMs
items.summary: A model-agnostic PII detection method is described, which uses large language models on Amazon Bedrock to identify and adapt to new entity types without retraining.

items.title: How a researcher uses Codex and ChatGPT to search for new antimicrobial molecules
items.summary: A researcher's lab is utilizing AI models like Codex and ChatGPT to identify new antimicrobial molecules by searching through living and extinct genomes.

items.title: Google expands India's clean-energy push with Solar API for 300M rooftops, climate-smart agri programme, and more
items.summary: Google is supporting Indian climate-tech startups that use AI, satellite imagery, and geospatial intelligence for applications like regenerative agriculture and carbon removal.

items.title: GFF 2026: Fintech-AI Partnerships Take The Centre Stage On Day 2
items.summary: This item discusses Fintech-AI partnerships taking center stage at a global fintech event, highlighting real-world applications of AI within the finance industry.

items.title: Grafista: Graphic design platform fighting AI slop
items.summary: Grafista is presented as a graphic design platform developed to combat the issue of low-quality or generic 'AI slop' in creative output.

items.title: Guiding AI writing to make technical text easier to review
items.summary: This article discusses methods for guiding AI writing to produce technical text that is easier to review and process.

items.title: Show HN: AI Brand Visibility for Free Forever
items.summary: A new tool called 'AI Brand Visibility' offers free comprehensive analysis of what shows up in LLM searches related to a user's brand.

items.title: Show HN: Swiftcruit – AI assisted technical assessment platform
items.summary: Swiftcruit is an AI-assisted platform for technical assessments that generates real-world problems from job descriptions and provides detailed scorecards, including evaluation of AI proficiency.

items.title: What we learnt from OpenAI’s hack of Hugging Face
items.summary: This article analyzes lessons learned from a security incident involving OpenAI's interaction with Hugging Face, highlighting the failure of commercial AI tools and suggesting open-weight models as a solution.

items.title: Show HN: Oracle Forms to Java: A Two-Week AI Migration Experiment
items.summary: This article describes an experiment demonstrating the use of AI to migrate Oracle Forms applications to Java within a two-week timeframe.

items.title: Show HN: Security Cards – Reducing insecure AI-generated code by 72%
items.summary: Researchers have open-sourced 'Security Cards,' a method offering targeted security guidance for libraries, which significantly reduces the rate of insecure code generated by AI coding agents.

items.title: Top News Today: India's Chips, Europe's AI Funding, Karnataka Jobs & Crypto Rules
Clearview AI Is Testing an AI Tool That Would Let Cops Unearth Your Life Online
items.summary: Clearview AI is testing an AI tool called InquiryIQ, which leverages an xAI model to gather extensive online information about individuals for law enforcement purposes. This describes a new application of AI technology.

items.title: Wipro's AI push frees capacity equivalent to 20,000 workers, CTO says - Reuters
items.summary: Wipro's CTO stated that the company's AI initiatives have freed up capacity equivalent to 20,000 workers, demonstrating AI's impact on operational efficiency in industry. This highlights a practical application of AI in a business setting.

items.title: Healthcare AI’s next test is integration
items.summary: The healthcare sector is seeing increased integration of AI, with advanced models capable of processing clinical records and complex medical terminology. This highlights the growing real-world applications and challenges of AI in healthcare.

items.title: GFF 2026: Mahindra Finance scales Sarvam voice AI partnership to 1 crore calls across 12 languages - The Economic Times
items.summary: Mahindra Finance is expanding its partnership with Sarvam voice AI to handle 10 million calls in 12 languages. This demonstrates a large-scale real-world application of AI in the financial services industry.

items.title: Beyond Right and Wrong: Evaluating Second-order Social Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper investigates evaluating second-order social reasoning in large language models, moving beyond first-order social norm recognition to anticipating enforcement and social dynamics.

items.title: Damage-Aware Bandit Pruning for Vision and Language Transformers
items.summary: This research proposes a damage-aware bandit pruning method for vision and language transformers to selectively remove functional units while limiting model degradation.

items.title: Compiling VGDL into Causal Models
items.summary: This research explores compiling Video Game Description Language (VGDL) into causal models to improve how reinforcement learning and large language models capture causal mechanics in game environments.

items.title: RAPID: Reliability-Aware Pair Importance Distillation
items.summary: RAPID (Reliability-Aware Pair Importance Distillation) is introduced as a method to efficiently transfer a teacher model's representation geometry by focusing on important relationships among examples.

items.title: Reasoning-Aware Compression: Identifying and Protecting Vulnerable Reasoning Circuits for Energy-Efficient LLM Deployment
items.summary: This paper introduces a reasoning-aware compression framework designed to identify and protect critical reasoning circuits in large language models for more energy-efficient deployment.

items.title: The Failure Happens Before the Drift: The Social Dynamics of Values in LLM Agent Societies
items.summary: This research presents a World Values Survey (WVS)-grounded simulation framework to investigate the social dynamics of values in LLM agent societies.

items.title: The convergent laboratory: when AI reasoning, autonomous experiments, high performance and quantum computing reshape chemistry
items.summary: This article discusses how AI reasoning, autonomous agents, and high-performance computing are converging to reshape chemistry and materials science discovery. It stems from a conference focused on these applications.

items.title: Distilling Vision-Language Models for On-Device Fire Understanding
items.summary: This research investigates distilling vision-language models (VLMs) for on-device fire understanding to enable practical deployment on embedded fire sensors despite their large model size.

items.title: More Than Mimicking Reviewers: Evaluating LLMs for Pre-Submission Peer Review
items.summary: This study evaluates LLMs for pre-submission peer review, developing an author-facing system that generates and compresses concerns into a report, and assessing its agreement with historical reviews.

items.title: Evidence-Aligned Local Composition of Discrete Experts for Sequence Restoration
items.summary: This paper describes a method for evidence-aligned local composition of discrete experts to perform sequence restoration on corrupted documents composed of texts from different domains.

items.title: Exposing Weaknesses in Emotion Recognition in Conversations
items.summary: This research exposes weaknesses in current Emotion Recognition in Conversations (ERC) methods, which aim to identify emotions in multi-turn dialogues for applications like empathetic conversational agents.

items.title: Learning Counterfactual World Models for Embodied Reasoning under Partial Observability
items.summary: This research explores learning counterfactual world models for embodied reasoning under partial observability, aiming to build predictive dynamics for embodied intelligence.

items.title: Multimodal Resource-Exhaustion Attacks on Vision-Language Models via Joint Pixel-Prompt Optimization
items.summary: This research presents multimodal resource-exhaustion attacks on vision-language models (VLMs) through joint pixel-prompt optimization, exposing vulnerabilities in these systems.

items.title: Generating Instance Generators in PDDL Planning
items.summary: This research explores methods for generating instance generators within PDDL, the standard language for AI planning, to better specify actual instance sets and legality constraints.

items.title: CWF: A Collaborative Writing Framework for Personalized and Reliable Popular Science Writing
items.summary: CWF is a collaborative writing framework designed for personalized and reliable popular science writing, adapting scientific explanations to different cognitive levels while preserving factual accuracy.

items.title: IIns-VAE+: A Robust Transfer Learning Framework for Environmental Identification in Wireless Sensing
items.summary: IIns-VAE+ is a robust transfer learning framework designed for environmental identification in wireless sensing, aiming to improve the generalization of deep learning models under domain shift for 6G ISAC systems.

items.title: MVFA: A Multi-View Text-Guided Multimodal Fusion LLM Adapter for Sentiment Analysis and Emotion Recognition
items.summary: MVFA is a multi-view text-guided multimodal fusion LLM adapter designed to enhance sentiment analysis and emotion recognition in conversations by effectively modeling heterogeneous interactions across textual, acoustic, and visual modalities.

items.title: Predicting Wind Turbine Power Using Machine Learning and Weather Forecasts
items.summary: This research explores using machine learning and weather forecasts to accurately predict offshore wind turbine power, aiming to optimize maintenance scheduling for renewable energy generation.

items.title: HB-PVI: A Hierarchical Bayesian Personalization and Value-of-Information Framework for Complex Activity Recognition
items.summary: This paper introduces HB-PVI, a hierarchical Bayesian framework designed for personalizing complex activity recognition. It jointly models personalization and value-of-information to improve performance while considering calibration costs.

items.title: Endogenous Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Curiosity
items.summary: This research proposes a reinforcement learning framework that uses intrinsic curiosity to drive exploration, particularly in environments with sparse or uninformative rewards. Action selection in this model is guided by a combination of external rewards.

items.title: Robustness of LLM-Generated SystemVerilog Assertions to Semantics-Preserving RTL Transformations
items.summary: This study investigates the robustness of SystemVerilog Assertions generated by large language models against semantics-preserving RTL transformations. It examines whether an LLM's correct output remains stable when the input is syntactically varied.

items.title: PAC-Private Autoregressive Generation: Calibrating Noise to Ensemble Disagreement
items.summary: This paper introduces PAC-Private Autoregressive Generation, a method to protect privacy when language models adapted on private text are served via APIs. It addresses privacy leakage through generated outputs by calibrating noise based on ensemble disagreement.

items.title: Connecting Score Matching, Maximum Likelihood, and Expectation-Maximization in Mixed Linear Regression
items.summary: This study analyzes the connections between score matching, maximum likelihood, and expectation-maximization within the context of mixed linear regression. It investigates variance-preserving diffusion of responses with unknown mixing weights.

items.title: GraphNOSE: A Graph Transformer in Olfaction
items.summary: This paper introduces GraphNOSE, a Graph Transformer model designed to predict olfactory qualities directly from molecular structures. This aims to overcome limitations of traditional linear models in chemoinformatics, particularly for novel or complex molecules.

items.title: Analysis of Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia with Neural Networks
items.summary: This paper introduces a neural network-based approach for analyzing ECG signals to estimate respiratory rate by leveraging Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia. The deep learning model is trained to predict respiratory waveforms directly from ECG input data.

items.title: Newton Matching for Generative Modeling: A Unified Framework for Fine-Tuning and Sampling
items.summary: This paper develops Newton Matching, a unified framework for both fine-tuning and sampling within generative modeling. It targets a distribution proportional to a reward-exponentiated pretrained model density.

items.title: A Multi-Source Ensemble Approach to Candidate Generation for Alternative Vacation Rental Property Recommendations
items.summary: This paper proposes a multi-source ensemble approach for generating candidate alternative recommendations in vacation rental marketplaces. The method aims to overcome challenges like heterogeneous inventory and geographic constraints to improve user discovery.

items.title: Data Scout: Targeted Web Crawling for Domain-Specific Pretraining Corpora
items.summary: This paper introduces Data Scout, a method for targeted web crawling to build domain-specific pretraining corpora, especially for specialized domains where content is sparse. It aims to overcome limitations of filtering large web archives like CommonCrawl.

items.title: RAPTOR: Role-Aware Private Training for Mixture-of-Experts
items.summary: This paper presents RAPTOR, a method for role-aware private training of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, addressing limitations of existing differentially private fine-tuning techniques. It characterizes failure modes that arise when treating MoE models as dense blocks.

items.title: Nonlinear elliptic homogenization with the parametric Deep Ritz method
items.summary: This paper applies the parametric Deep Ritz method to solve nonlinear elliptic homogenization problems in materials science. This approach determines coarse-grained properties of materials with small-scale features.

items.title: Generalizing HVAC Control With Domain Randomized Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This research proposes NOMAD-RL, a general-purpose reinforcement learning framework using domain randomization to generalize HVAC control. This approach aims to overcome the need for accurate building models or per-site retuning for scalable deployment.

items.title: Grounded and Faithful P&ID Reasoning: Constraining Vision-Language Models with Recovered Evidence Graphs
items.summary: This paper proposes a method to achieve grounded and faithful P&ID reasoning by constraining vision-language models with recovered evidence graphs. This approach aims to prevent models from inventing or missing critical process connections in industrial diagrams.

items.title: One Rate Is Not Enough: Adaptive Anisotropic Learning Rates for LoRA Fine-Tuning
items.summary: This paper proposes using adaptive anisotropic learning rates for LoRA fine-tuning of large language models, arguing against the conventional uniform learning rate. This method aims to improve parameter-efficient fine-tuning by allowing different learning rates for adapter components.

items.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Efficiency Methods for Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: This paper rethinks the evaluation of efficiency methods for Large Language Model-based multi-agent systems. It addresses the challenge of substantial execution costs by examining existing approaches for pruning agents and optimizing communication.

items.title: QGB-W$k$NN: Quantum Granular-Ball Learning for Robust Classification
items.summary: This paper introduces QGB-WkNN, a quantum granular-ball learning method for robust classification that aims to improve computational efficiency and robustness of K-nearest neighbor algorithms. It addresses challenges faced by existing methods in noisy environments.

items.title: On-the-go Forgetting without Explicit Unlearning via ERASE
items.summary: This paper introduces ERASE, a framework for "on-the-go forgetting" in AI models, allowing for unlearning without explicit post hoc weight adaptation or distillation. It aims to reduce memory costs and improve generalization compared to existing unlearning approaches.

items.title: Machine Learning for Pre-Culture ESBL Risk Stratification to Guide Empiric Antibiotic Selection: A 12-Hospital Study of Enterobacteriaceae Cultures
items.summary: Researchers developed a cost-sensitive XGBoost machine learning model for pre-culture ESBL risk stratification in Enterobacteriaceae cultures, tested across 12 hospitals. This AI application aims to guide empiric antibiotic selection, balancing the risks of undertreatment and overuse.

items.title: IXPLORE: Bounded Ideal Point Estimation with Grid-Based Uncertainty Quantification
items.summary: This paper introduces IXPLORE, a method for bounded ideal point estimation with grid-based uncertainty quantification, primarily used for analyzing and visualizing political data. It addresses trade-offs in selecting spatial models like Item Response Theory.

items.title: Minimizing the Effect of Sleep Deprivation in the Forward-Forward Algorithm
items.summary: This paper investigates how to minimize the effects of "sleep deprivation" in the Forward-Forward algorithm, conceptualizing imbalanced data processing during its passes as an imitation of cognitive processes in sleep-deprived humans. It presents a novel approach to address this challenge.

items.title: Data Quality Rule Generation with LLMs
items.summary: This research explores using Large Language Models (LLMs) for generating data quality rules, an important task for validating organizational data like customer or employee records. This application aims to prevent severe consequences from data errors.

items.title: Calendar-SPCA: Interpretable Representation Learning for Multi-Periodic Electricity Consumption Profiles
items.summary: This work introduces Calendar-SPCA, a calendar-structured sparse principal component method for interpretable representation learning applied to multi-periodic electricity consumption profiles. It incorporates known daily, weekly, and annual periodic geometries into the analysis.

items.title: ACE: Adapter Consolidation across Experts for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of MoE LLMs
items.summary: This paper proposes ACE (Adapter Consolidation across Experts), a method to improve Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs. It addresses the fragmentation of adaptation capacity and gradient supervision caused by expert-wise adapter designs.

items.title: FedSubMuon: Communication-Efficient Federated LLM Fine-Tuning via Structured Subspace Muon
items.summary: This paper introduces FedSubMuon, a method for communication-efficient federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) using a structured subspace Muon optimizer. It aims to improve scalability by reducing high communication costs in cross-device training.

items.title: Beyond Retraining-Free MoE Compression: A Cost-Normalized Study of Post-Compression Adjustment
items.summary: This paper presents a cost-normalized study on post-compression adjustment for retraining-free Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) compression, which aims to reduce deployment memory by pruning or merging experts. It argues that compressed MoE checkpoints can benefit from further adjustment.

items.title: Connectome-to-Function: Conditional Generative Latent Representations for Reservoir Computing
items.summary: This research explores "Connectome-to-Function" by developing conditional generative latent representations for reservoir computing, aiming to understand how brain circuits support function and computation. It addresses the challenge of mapping high-dimensional connectome structures to computational processes.

items.title: VERPO: Verified Evidence Regularized Policy Optimization
items.summary: This paper introduces VERPO (Verified Evidence Regularized Policy Optimization), a method that guides language-model post-training using verifiable outcome rewards. It aims to provide denser supervision by identifying which token-level decisions should be preserved or revised using evidence-conditioned teachers.

items.title: FANS: Federated Adaptive Network Search Learning for Heterogeneous Devices
items.summary: This paper introduces FANS (Federated Adaptive Network Search Learning), a method designed for heterogeneous federated learning across devices with diverse resource budgets while preserving data privacy. It aims to overcome limitations of predefined model configurations by expanding architectural coverage.

items.title: Rethinking One-Shot Federated Graph Learning: Training-Free Statistical Estimation
items.summary: This paper rethinks one-shot federated graph learning by proposing a training-free statistical estimation method for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) across clients with disconnected subgraphs. It challenges the premise that local GNN training is indispensable in this paradigm.

items.title: All for 1-Bit: Towards Genuine 1-Bit Post-Training Quantization for LLMs
items.summary: This paper investigates "Genuine 1-Bit Post-Training Quantization" for Large Language Models (LLMs) to address their massive storage and memory-bandwidth demands hindering efficient deployment. It explores weight binarization as a promising solution.

items.title: Decision-Aware Suffix Prediction and Reasoning of Business Processes
items.summary: This research proposes a "Decision-Aware Suffix Prediction and Reasoning" method for business processes, which forecasts the remaining sequence of events using neural networks trained on event logs. It aims to improve prediction accuracy, especially for short prefixes or rare process variants.

items.title: Spectral Prioritized Sweeping in Nonstationary Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This research introduces a method called Spectral Prioritized Sweeping to accelerate model-based reinforcement learning, specifically addressing its limitations in nonstationary reward settings.

items.title: EgoNeMo: Transferable Map of Pedestrian Dynamics via Egocentric LiDAR Scan
items.summary: This paper proposes EgoNeMo, a transferable Map of Dynamics framework that uses egocentric 3D LiDAR point clouds to generalize pedestrian dynamics to unknown environments, overcoming traditional MoD limitations.

items.title: X-CoSD: Communication-Efficient Cross-Vocabulary Collaborative Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This paper explores X-CoSD, a communication-efficient collaborative speculative decoding framework for distributed large language model inference, where an on-device small model drafts tokens and a server LLM verifies them.

items.title: Osprey: Target-agnostic Pre-training Makes Stronger Drafters in Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This research introduces Osprey, a method for pre-training stronger drafters for speculative decoding in LLM inference, aiming to make speedup less fragile and more robust to workload shifts.

items.title: Auditable Emergency Triage for Maternal and Newborn Care in India
items.summary: Noora Health developed an auditable AI system for emergency triage in maternal and newborn care in India, supporting nurses on their WhatsApp-based service for time-critical medical queries.

items.title: Do LLMs Make More Mistakes If They Do Not Believe the Input Data?
items.summary: This research analyzes how the faithfulness of large language models to provided context depends on their perceived plausibility of the input data, addressing issues like hallucination in RAG systems.

items.title: Edu-QuRating: Multi-Dimensional Educational Data Curation with Distilled Pairwise Judgements
items.summary: This paper proposes Edu-QuRating, a multi-dimensional educational data curation method using distilled pairwise judgments to improve language model pre-training beyond simple scalar educational value.

items.title: TEFM: Token-Efficient Faithful Modeling for Structured Data
items.summary: This paper presents TEFM (Token-Efficient Faithful Modeling), a new framework designed to address token efficiency and faithfulness challenges when applying large language models to structured data in critical domains.

items.title: Towards Automatic Evolution Tree Generation from Citation Graphs
items.summary: This research explores methods for automatically generating evolution trees from citation graphs, aiming to provide a scalable way for researchers to understand the lineage of methods within AI subfields.

items.title: Reproducing Omitted Temporal Expressions in Japanese News for Retrieval-Augmented Applications
items.summary: This research addresses the problem of reproducing omitted temporal expressions in Japanese news articles for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications, which often misinterpret standalone text.

items.title: Beyond Top Words: MonoTM for Topic Modeling with Interpretable Monosemantic Features
items.summary: This paper introduces MonoTM, a new topic modeling approach that uses interpretable monosemantic features extracted by sparse autoencoders, moving beyond traditional top-word summaries.

items.title: X2-NativeCursor: Native-Token Text Progress Tracking for Incremental-Text Streaming Codec TTS
items.summary: This paper presents X2-NativeCursor, a method for native-token text progress tracking in incremental-text streaming codec text-to-speech (TTS) systems, enabling synchronized highlighting and better dialogue management.

items.title: Looped GPT-BERT: Trading Parameters for Computation in Small Language Modeling
items.summary: This research investigates Looped GPT-BERT, a small language modeling approach that trades parameter count for computation by repeatedly applying a smaller parameter set to achieve comparable performance.

items.title: When Auditors Fabricate: Batch-Size Degradation and Confident Hallucination in LLM Detection of Planted Document Contamination
items.summary: Large language models are increasingly proposed as automated auditors of document quality, yet their reliability as detectors of planted errors is poorly characterised. We construct a contaminated corpus of 150 academic papers spanning supply chain management and medical research, injecting 450 known contaminants of three types: typographical corruption, semantic reversal, and absurd out-of-context insertion. We then evaluate Google Gemini 3.0 Pro's ability to recover a 180-contaminant answer-key subset across 60 documents under three prompting regimes of increasing scale: single document, small batch, and large batch. Detection holds at small scale and then collapses: 50% recovery on single documents, 60% on small batches, and 2.8% on large batches. The failure mode at scale is not abstention but fabrication. Rather than reporting incomplete processing, the model produced confident findings including invented contaminants of its own, absurdities such as "telepathic squirrel" and "quantum-powered toaster" that mimic the style of the planted material but do not appear in any document. Detection also varies by contamination type: absurd insertions were recovered at 75% in completed evaluations, while semantic reversals and typographical corruptions were each recovered at only 50%. The corruptions most likely to occur in the wild, plausible ones, are the ones most often missed. We conclude that LLM document auditing degrades not gracefully but deceptively, and outline the harness such systems require: bounded batch sizes, direct content injection, and mechanical verification of every reported finding against source text.

items.title: Scaling E-Commerce Attribute Extraction with Parallel Decoding
items.summary: Customers rely on specific product attributes to compare products and make purchasing decisions, but e-commerce catalogs are messy and unstructured, making it difficult to identify which attributes matter most and extract them at scale. Standard Attribute Value Extraction (AVE) systems treat all attributes equally, producing large, inconsistent attribute sets that do not reflect the factors consumers use to differentiate products. We introduce a two-stage LLM pipeline that first discovers a compact, ranked schema of purchase-discriminative attributes for each product category, then extracts their values from catalog text using a fine-tuned compact LLM (Qwen3-4B) with Hyper-Parallel Decoding (HPD). This pipeline achieves 85% extraction accuracy, on par with the foundational LLM it was distilled from, while reducing inference costs by 92% over foundational LLMs, enabling production-scale use for product discovery and catalog enrichment. The resulting category-level structured representations effectively constitute automatically constructed product knowledge bases, providing consistent, comparable attributes across varied product categories that can ground downstream knowledge-intensive applications.

items.title: StreamAlign: Streaming Text-Aligned Speech Tokenization
items.summary: Text-aligned speech tokenization methods have emerged to better align speech tokens with LLM token spaces, enabling more effective utilization of pretrained LLMs. However, they rely on offline automatic speech recognition (ASR), leading to two key limitations: (i) the need for complete utterances before tokenization, precluding real-time streaming, and (ii) vocabulary mismatch between ASR and LLMs, which reduces acoustic granularity from the subword to the word level. We introduce StreamAlign, a text-aligned speech tokenization framework that enables streaming tokenization for real-time speech-text joint modeling. StreamAlign performs online speech-text alignment by combining character-level RNN-Transducer alignment with word-level ASR guidance, mitigating ASR-LLM vocabulary mismatch while preserving recognition accuracy. A proactive word boundary classifier anticipates word completion at chunk boundaries, reducing tokenization latency from 560 ms to 270 ms. On LibriSpeech, StreamAlign achieves the lowest WER and highest UTMOS among evaluated tokenizers. Furthermore, StreamAlign-SLM, a spoken language model trained on StreamAlign units, outperforms other end-to-end spoken language models in speech continuation while achieving the strongest overall consistency on SALMon and spoken StoryCloze.

items.title: SocialRL: Refining LLMs' Social Intelligence through Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning and Reward Design
items.summary: Social intelligence enables agents to read social context, infer intent, and adapt over sustained dialogue. As language models become autonomous collaborators, it is central to building effective and trustworthy human-AI interaction. Existing reinforcement learning methods optimize single-turn utterances and sparse outcome rewards, producing short-sighted policies that struggle to manage goal-relationship tensions across multi-turn interactions. We propose SocialRL, a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework addressing both challenges. First, we apply multi-turn reinforcement learning using PPO that propagates delayed outcome rewards back to each turn, enabling long-horizon planning. Second, we design six process reward dimensions capturing the goal-relationship trade-off, including goal advancement, relational attunement, contextual coherence, etc. A reward model dynamically generates fine-grained scoring criteria for each dimension, while a stage-aware weight schedule prioritizes relationship-building in early turns, goal advancement mid-way, and balanced closure late. Across multiple social-dialogue benchmarks, SocialRL improves Goal Achievement by an average of 9.2 percentage points over the corresponding Base models. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SocialRL across synthetic and real social scenes, as well as standard and challenging social scenarios.

items.title: CARRE: Counterfactual Action Retrieval and Reason Evaluation for Explainable Churn Prescription
items.summary: Churn models typically identify high-risk customers but do not specify which feasible retention action should be considered or why that action is appropriate. We present CARRE (Counterfactual Action Retrieval and Reason Evaluation), a three-stage framework that combines retrieval-augmented candidate generation, cost-aware counterfactual scoring, and large language model (LLM) reasoning. CARRE retrieves a predefined catalog of retention actions, estimates model-predicted churn-risk changes under explicit feature transformations, and generates a structured churn reason and a profile-grounded explanation for the selected action. On the IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset, CARRE achieves 79.8% greater mean model-predicted risk reduction than the plain SHAP baseline and 80.4% greater reduction than the cost-controlled SHAP+Cost baseline across 313 high-risk test cases; its cost-normalized efficiency is 10.5% higher than that of plain SHAP. On a 136-case reason-stratified evaluation sample, diagnosis-driven prompt refinement increases weak-label agreement from 79.4% to 90.4%, with no auxiliary-plan constraint violations; because the same sample was used for error diagnosis and re-evaluation, the post-refinement result is not an independent estimate of generalization. For 135 explanations generated using the pre-refinement v2 reason outputs, two cross-vendor LLM judges assign mean scores ranging from 4.02 to 5.00 out of 5, although one judge saturates on actionability, and a deterministic audit finds no contradictions among 66 verifiable profile claims. Retrieval ablations show that k=5 provides the best evaluated compromise between high candidate coverage and downstream reasoning agreement in this dataset. These results illustrate how retrieval, model-based counterfactual scoring, and language generation can be separated and jointly evaluated in a prototype churn-prescription pipeline.

items.title: SymbolicLight V2: Hybrid Neuromorphic Architecture and Sparse Execution for Low-Energy Language Inference
items.summary: SymbolicLight V2 combines sparse event computation with continuous-state processing in a hybrid neuromorphic language architecture. Extending V1's spike-gated dual paths, it adds graded signed events at further projections and softmax-free local attention. We implement the 194M-parameter model on an Alveo U50C FPGA using digital fixed-point arithmetic and on an ARM CPU using sparse integer execution. Across three same-checkpoint FPGA implementations at 175 MHz, active-row weight gathering and valid-state KV loading raise decode throughput from 474.6 to 643.2 tokens/s for a 32-token prefix and 128 outputs. Estimated gross card energy falls from 0.06087 to 0.04407 J per generated token, a 27.6% reduction. Complete-request energy, including prefill, falls by 24.4-27.7% across three prefix lengths. An independent idle split attributes 82.8% of gross card energy to loaded idle, explaining the benefit of shorter token latency. Against the recorded RTX 5090 compiled-FP32 baseline, integer FPGA execution uses 89.1% less estimated card energy during short-context decode; arithmetic precisions differ, and the GPU baseline is not the lowest-energy tested configuration. On four Cortex-A76 cores of a ROCK 5T, complete requests reach 65.4 tokens/s at 9.80 W and 0.151 J per generated token at the adapter's AC input. These results connect event sparsity to omitted computation and data movement. The mechanisms also support other dedicated V2 implementations: increasing throughput by a greater factor than active power lowers energy per generated token. Evaluation holds the deployed checkpoint fixed; its quality trails a same-budget dense control, so the results do not establish equal-quality efficiency.

items.title: ROAM: Robust Organization of Atomic Memories for Agents through Semantic Relations
items.summary: Long-term language-model agents rely on external memory across interactions. Atomic memories are particularly useful: their fine-grained semantic boundaries enable precise retrieval and direct comparison between observations. Yet accumulating atoms inevitably become redundant, overlapping, or conflicting. Existing methods often ask an LLM manager to add, update, delete, or rewrite memories directly, coupling semantic interpretation, storage decisions, and content generation in one error-prone operation. We introduce ROAM, a relation-guided framework that uses atomicity for management while allowing richer answer-time representations. ROAM classifies incoming--stored atom pairs as independent, equivalent, directionally subsuming, or conflicting, then organizes observations into active Primary and supporting Evidence roles. Fusion subsequently combines complementary details and temporal changes into compact, potentially non-atomic views. Only Primary views are retrieved for answering, preventing redundant or outdated atoms from competing independently. Across models and evaluation settings, ROAM improves answer accuracy by up to 29.8 percentage points. Ablations show complementary benefits from different relations and consistent gains from fusion beyond role organization. Mechanism analysis further finds 15.6-point higher answer-critical source recall and an 11.5-point lower confounder-token share. ROAM remains robust across manager scales.

items.title: HyperTrace: Hypothesis-Based Preference Tracing for Online LLM Personalization
items.summary: Personalized language models aim to adapt responses to individual users, whose preferences are often latent and revealed gradually through interaction. Existing training-free methods rely on stored histories or retrieved memories, but they often struggle to reconcile long- term preferences with short-term topic-specific needs. To address this issue, we propose HyperTrace, a training-free framework that formulates online personalization as latent preference tracing. HyperTrace maintains interpretable natural-language hypotheses over short-term intent and long-term preferences, and updates them through an SMC-style reweight process using an LLM-based surrogate choice model. By updating these hypotheses across turns and sessions, HyperTrace enables personalization without parameter updates. Experiments on PRISM and PersonaMem-v2 show that HyperTrace improves response alignment, preference prediction, and profile consistency over strong online baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of tracing latent user preferences for robust personalization. Code and scripts are available in the repository: https://github.com/jiseshen/HyperTrace.

items.title: $S^3$-Bench: Evaluating Speech Interaction Models as Scientific Voice Assistants
items.summary: The advance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) has fundamentally reshaped the paradigm of human-computer interaction, especially speech interaction models capable of seamless conversations. Despite remarkable performance as general voice assistants, their performance in specialized domains remains underexplored, particularly in scientific areas. Scientific interactions introduce formidable challenges, involving rare technical terminology, spoken norms of abbreviations, and the natural verbalization of symbolic special expressions. In this paper, we introduce S$^3$-Bench, a systematic evaluation framework covering 10 major disciplines, consisting of a Knowledge set for speech question-answering and a Dialogue set for multi-turn progressive interactions with simulated user agents. By decomposing a complete atomic turn into stages of speech recognition, perception, knowledge utilization with reasoning, and response pronunciation, we systematically characterize the common challenges and performance tradeoffs of existing approaches. Furthermore, experiments on multi-turn interactions reveal persistent limitations in user adaptation and the generation of accurate, comprehensive, and efficient responses.

items.title: When Does Defendant Statement Matter? A Study of Bias and Persuasion in LLM-Simulated Jurors
items.summary: LLMs have been used to simulate human decision-making in professional settings, yet their behaviors in common-law jury trials remain unexplored. We study when and how a defendant's courtroom statement affects LLM-simulated jurors, focusing on persuasion, ideological bias, and background-based affinity. To support the analysis, we introduce JuryBench, a benchmark containing controversial criminal cases in U.S. criminal law. In each case, a defendant can claim various plausible justifications to support acquittal or reduced liability. We fix the base case and design defendants of different backgrounds, who give courtroom statements with varying emotional appeal or rebuttal. Jurors with diverse ideological profiles across the spectrum are simulated. We examine 20 frontier LLMs, resulting in a total of 432K decisions and rationales, and quantify changes in verdict severity. Our findings show that LLM-jury simulation echoes many human-jury findings. First, emotional persuasion can be detrimental, since jurors may perceive it as evidence of guilt or inconsistency. Next, we show that background fit between jurors and defendants is a stronger and significant factor than other isolated factors, and that jurors are in general harsher toward opposite-background defendants and lenient toward same-background ones. Finally, we find that juror ideology also strongly shapes severity judgments. These findings highlight both the promise and risks of using LLMs to model jury reasoning and call for careful evaluation. The data and code are available at https://github.com/choyingw/JuryBench

items.title: Leveraging Fine-grained Error Correction in Korean Speech Recognition for Consultation Services
items.summary: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) technology is fundamental to customer service automation and large-scale transcription. However, even advanced ASR models exhibit inevitable errors in complex real-world environments such as call center conversations. When privacy restrictions preclude audio access, error correction must rely on text-based post-editing. Existing text-only approaches face significant challenges in low-resource languages, mainly due to a critical scarcity of annotated corpora and tailored correction methodologies. For Korean, this resource gap is particularly pronounced, as existing resources are predominantly designed for ASR training rather than text-based error correction. To address this, we introduce DasanCallDial, the first large-scale Korean benchmark dataset specifically curated for dialogue-level ASR error correction. Derived from genuine call center interactions, it comprises 1,974 dialogues with 115,460 utterances. Leveraging this resource, we propose Detector-Gated Contextual Span Correction (DCSC), a text-only post-editing framework for error-sparse Korean speech recognition transcripts. DCSC combines an encoder-based detector that first performs token-level error detection, followed by a language model-based corrector trained to rectify fine-grained span-level errors. Additionally, we employ dialogue-level context augmentation to enable the model to leverage discourse history for disambiguation. By employing multi-level granularity, our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, effectively overcoming the limitations of general LLMs in low-resource settings.

items.title: Deep and shallow biases in language models
items.summary: Large language models often repeatedly select the same answer even when many alternatives are plausible. Prior work treats this concentration as bias, but it does not distinguish stable model preferences from responses that depend on a particular prompt wording. We introduce a bias depth score that measures both how strongly a model prefers its top answer under direct prompting and whether that answer survives scenario reframing. Across 4,442 opinion prompts and four large language models, only about a quarter of the concentrated preferences survive reframing. We call these persistent cases Deep biases, and the remaining prompt-dependent cases Shallow biases. Our results show that Deep biases are more often inherited from pretraining and preserved through SFT. Under both continued fine-tuning and prompt-based debiasing for diversity, Deep biases are consistently harder to remove than Shallow biases. Bias depth therefore separates stable learned biases from prompt-wording artifacts that single-prompt metrics conflate. Code, models, and data are available at deepbias.github.io.

items.title: Contrastive Projection: Reading Transformer Internals by Differencing Logit Lenses
items.summary: Reading a transformer's internal states in token space is easy to do and hard to trust: a logit lens on a single hidden state is dominated, at intermediate layers, by the generic tokens the model would predict for almost any input. We read the difference instead. Subtracting two closely matched prompts' hidden states and projecting through the unembedding cancels the shared component and surfaces what separates them, an operation equivalent to reading a RepE/ActAdd steering vector through a logit lens. Built into a training-free tracer that reads at every position, sub-layer, and head and averages over designed baselines, it traces a compound- noun MLP->attention chain in Phi-2, confirmed there by activation patching, with the same distinction recovered across three architectures by readout and probe rather than by patching; it reads what retrieval surfaces for real versus fictional entities, and reads metaphor as a set of domain-to-domain mappings rather than a single figurativity feature. A cross-seed control marks the boundary: across five networks differing only in initialization, the same distinction surfaces as almost entirely different tokens (top-10 overlap 0.08). What a computation looks like in token space is network-specific; the distinction it draws is not

items.title: Improving Cross-Lingual Token Representations by Adding a Pinch of SALT
items.summary: Cross-lingual sentence encoders enable scalable transfer across hundreds of languages, powering applications such as translation mining and zero-shot learning in low-resource settings. Although trained for sentence-level alignment, they are increasingly also applied to token-level tasks such as hallucination detection and sequence tagging, exposing a mismatch between training and usage. We propose SALT, a lightweight post-training method that improves token representations by injecting span-level supervision into existing sentence encoders. Across five multilingual token-level benchmarks, SALT achieves the best overall results on four of them, outperforming alternative fine-tuning strategies and competitive encoders. It also improves sentence-level performance on cross-lingual retrieval and classification tasks. These results demonstrate that span-level supervision is an effective signal for improving both token and sentence representations.

items.title: 5-Dialects-BN: Unmasking the Impact of Transliteration on Bangla Dialectal LLMs
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress across natural language processing (NLP) tasks, yet their capabilities degrade sharply for low-resource languages and dialectally diverse settings. Bangla, the world's sixth most spoken language, exemplifies this gap: existing resources overwhelmingly target Standard Bangla, leaving its regional dialects without the benchmarks needed to develop or evaluate dialect-aware systems. We address this gap with 5-Dialects-BN, the first multi-annotation Bangla dialect benchmark to align Romanized transliteration with dialectal text, Standard Bangla, English, and subjectivity labels across five regional varieties. The dataset comprises 6,000 manually annotated entries spanning five major dialects: Chittagong, Barisal, Noakhali, Sylhet, and Rangpur (Chittagong 1,900; Noakhali 1,500; Sylhet 1,200; Barisal 700; Rangpur 700), reflecting natural online availability. Each entry is enriched with five aligned annotations: the original dialectal text, a Romanized transliteration, an English translation, a Standard Bangla translation, and a subjectivity label (subjective vs. objective). Annotations were produced and cross-validated by native speakers and undergraduate linguistics students to ensure dialectal authenticity and semantic fidelity. The resulting resource supports a diverse suite of tasks, including dialect identification, dialect-to-standard normalization, machine translation, subjectivity classification, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA) of multilingual LLMs. By providing a standardized, multi-annotation benchmark, 5-Dialects-BN enables principled evaluation of LLMs on dialectally diverse Bangla and lays a foundation for further research in low-resource, dialect-aware NLP.

items.title: Towards Stress-Aware Sentence-Level Filipino G2P With Weakly-Supervised ByT5 Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Grapheme-to-phoneme conversion (G2P) refers to the task of converting a sequence of graphemes to a corresponding sequence of phonemes. While Filipino G2P is fairly straightforward due to its shallow orthography, the inclusion of prosodic features such as stress adds a layer of complexity that requires sentence-level context instead of single-word inputs. However, sentence-level data for Filipino typically do not include phoneme transcriptions, posing a challenge for training G2P models. As such, we investigate how to obtain sentence-level phoneme data for Filipino using available data and compare the resulting models with multilingual word-level G2P as well as measure how accurately they predict stress marker position for Filipino. We propose fine-tuning a ByT5-based model, pre-trained on multilingual word-level G2P data, on three sentence-level G2P datasets annotated with an LLM-assisted pipeline guided by data from Wiktionary. This approach produces models that perform well on the G2P task, achieving at best around 0.54% PER and 2.50% CER, a significant decrease compared to base model PER at around 19.74%, on a manually-corrected test set. The model is able to correctly classify most of the main stress classes in Filipino, but struggles particularly with malumi words. We show that a ByT5-based model performs well at sentence-level Filipino G2P and offers strong potential for Filipino homograph disambiguation.

items.title: Multi-Functional Embedding Models for Funder Name Disambiguation in Scientific Publication Records
items.summary: Understanding the historical allocation and distribution of research funding advances our knowledge of how scientific research is supported across fields, institutions, and regions. However, large-scale analyses are hindered by the lack of comprehensive funder name disambiguation solutions, as funder names often exhibit spelling variations, translations, abbreviations, and inconsistent levels of granularity. In this paper, we present a framework for developing multilingual, multi-functional funder name disambiguation models and demonstrate its application to research publications in biodiversity conservation. To construct a training dataset, we integrated the Research Organization Registry (ROR), which provides unique identifiers for research organizations, with two publication datasets: the Web of Science (WoS) and the Crossref Open Funder Registry (OFR). We used multi-task learning with Contrastive Loss and Multiple Negatives Ranking Loss to fine-tune three open-weight embedding models from the Sentence Transformer, Gemma, and Qwen3 families. The best-performing models achieved accuracy above 0.90 when matching WoS funder names to ROR identifiers, outperforming general-purpose LLMs, including GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, and Gemini-2.5-Flash, by more than 0.1. For funder names not indexed in ROR, we constructed a similarity network among funder names and identified clusters within it. Finally, we analyzed the disambiguation results and highlighted challenges arising from limited knowledge of smaller funders and funders from non-English-speaking countries. This work provides a reusable framework for funder name disambiguation with potential applicability across different model architectures and datasets, featuring cost-effective training data creation and multi-task learning and disambiguation.

items.title: VLX-VR: An Agentic-Aware Video Reasoning Model
items.summary: Real-world video understanding requires integrating visual, audio, textual, and temporal evidence distributed across a video. Yet many pipelines use a fixed video context and single-pass inference, limiting adaptive evidence acquisition when observations are incomplete, ambiguous, or conflicting. We present VLX-VR, an agentic-aware video reasoning model trained within a video reasoning framework defined by a Think--Memory--Observation loop. At each step, VLX-VR determines the needed evidence, invokes read_memory or write_memory, incorporates the returned Observation, and decides whether to continue or produce the task output. We train VLX-VR with multimodal data, including videos and agent trajectories, using reinforcement learning to learn evidence acquisition, memory use, and termination. On MINERVA, VLX-VR achieves state-of-the-art performance among the models included in our comparison, with 78.79% accuracy. Under the original three duration groups, its accuracies are 76.70%, 78.73%, and 80.92%, with a cross-duration accuracy variance of 2.97~$\mathrm{pp}^2$. On correctly answered samples, 96.20% of VLX-VR's reasoning traces are consistent with the MINERVA reference reasoning traces and the evidence described by them, while approximately 75.80% of all evaluated samples satisfy both answer correctness and this evidence-grounded trace criterion. These results show strong performance and broadly stable behavior across durations, while counting, state changes, causal reasoning, and spatial perception remain challenging.

items.title: Stable Answers, Unfinished Reasoning: Why Self-Consensus Is Not a Safe Early-Exit Signal
items.summary: A natural way to cut reasoning-model inference cost is to repeatedly probe a single partial trajectory for its current answer and stop once probes agree -- self-consensus. We ask whether any such rule is both safe and token-saving, and whether one can be selected once and reused. A preregistered sweep of 3,520 consensus rules, replayed on frozen trajectories from two models and three benchmarks, clears none of three acceptance gates fixed in advance; the frontier reproduces on a held-out split and on two unseen models -- while a boundary-confidence control (DEER) swept through the same pipeline clears all three. The reason lies in the signal: agreement establishes that the current answer persists under a fixed probing procedure, not that the reasoning has terminated -- a consensus-termination gap. Stopping on it commits non-terminal answers. At a rule still saving 32% of the tokens, one stop in nine fires on an answer the trajectory itself later abandons, and most of those stops cut off a correction it would otherwise have made. Widening the agreement window does not remove them: the share levels off near 7%, and by then the saving has fallen to 8%. Probe re-wording and a hand-labelled error taxonomy show the agreed answer is often a placeholder the model had not settled on. Used on its own as the stop signal, agreement fails not because it is insufficiently strict, but because it repeatedly measures the wrong object.

items.title: SalamandraTA at WMT 2026 Terminology Shared Task: Hard Examples Are Better Teachers
items.summary: Terminology-aware translation asks for more than a correct translation: the output must use the exact terms a glossary prescribes. The standard recipe, fine-tuning on glossary-annotated translation pairs, hides an inefficiency: for most examples the glossary prescribes exactly what the model would have produced anyway, so they teach nothing about following a glossary. We therefore keep only the examples where the model's own translation contradicts the glossary. In a controlled study at fixed data volume, this selection alone raises term accuracy from 78.7% to 89.9%. The filtered data, built by a two-way synthetic pipeline on open models, is part of the instruction-tuning mixture of our public release SalamandraTA-7b-instruct v3.0, which, used exactly as released and wrapped in a document-level inference pipeline, forms the BSC submission to the WMT26 Terminology Shared Task Track 1. At the official WMT26 evaluation, our system achieves 94.2% term success at 74.6 chrF++, with only two of the twenty-two submissions outperforming it on both metrics. On last year's benchmark, it also surpasses our GRPO-based system, despite being trained solely with ordinary supervised fine-tuning.

items.title: MedDeID enables locally governed clinical-text de-identification from real or synthetic training data
items.summary: Clinical notes contain personally identifiable information (PII), restricting reuse for research and medical AI, especially when data cannot leave an institution. We developed MedDeID, an on-premises framework combining in-house annotation and synthetic-note generation with model training, inference, pseudonymisation and evaluation. On an independently annotated, adjudicated 300-note Dutch hospital benchmark, a hospital-trained compact transformer detected 98.9% of identifying text while redacting 0.24% of text outside annotated identifiers; a synthetic-only counterpart detected 96.1%. On 100 primary-care notes, the synthetic-trained model achieved higher recall than the hospital-trained model (90.3% versus 87.0%) and greater robustness to identifier-format perturbations. An English instantiation trained without real text detected 99.7% and 98.9% of annotated identifier characters on two external synthetic benchmarks. These results demonstrate transfer of the workflow to another language, but not clinical English performance. MedDeID provides a route to locally governed de-identification using real or synthetic training data.

items.title: Direct Diversity Optimization for Diverse Successful Trajectories in Preference Post-Training
items.summary: LLM agents for sequential decision tasks are often post-trained with trajectory-level outcome labels, but such labels provide little supervision for preserving multiple successful branches from the same decision state. We study this problem as successful strategy coverage: how broadly a model realizes distinct successful strategies under a fixed rollout budget. We present Direct Diversity Optimization (DDO), an offline post-training method that combines Divergence-Tree Collection (DTC) with the Reference-Relative Target-Odds Objective (RTO). DTC constructs state-aligned branch sets rooted at shared decision states, and RTO trains the model to match reference-relative targets over successful alternatives. DDO achieves the strongest task success and successful strategy coverage among the compared post-training methods across BabyAI, BabaIsAI, and WebShop. It also achieves the highest recovery rate after local action replacement and higher task success and coverage than successful-only imitation and decoding-time diversification controls.

items.title: Data-Centric Post-Training for Financial Reasoning: Mining, Distillation, and Verifiable Learning
items.summary: Financial text, textbooks, and question-answer pairs are abundant, but only a small fraction is directly usable for reasoning-focused post-training. Existing QA pairs often lack explicit reasoning, sufficient context, or reliably verifiable answers, while textbooks must first be transformed into synthetic training examples.
