items.summary: This item analyzes that the adoption of AI in the workplace is currently widespread but lacks depth in its implementation and impact.

items.title: Climbers rescued on Mount Shasta after using AI chatbot to plan trip
items.summary: Climbers on Mount Shasta were rescued after using an AI chatbot to plan their trip, highlighting a real-world application and potential risks of relying on such tools.

items.title: Show HN: MRDown – a Mac Markdown app that diffs what your AI just rewrote
items.summary: MRDown is a Mac Markdown application designed to show diffs of text that has been rewritten by an AI.

items.title: Why AI food looks like that
items.summary: The article discusses the poor quality and unappetizing appearance of AI-generated images used by restaurants and brands to promote food.

items.title: AI Use in the Job Market Is Creating an Infinite Doom Loop
items.summary: AI use in the job market is creating an 'infinite doom loop' as job seekers attempt to game the application process with AI, leading to unintended consequences.

items.title: AI Powered Advanced Executive Program in Cybersecurity, IIIT Bangalore
items.summary: IIIT Bangalore is offering an advanced executive program in Cybersecurity that is powered by AI, demonstrating the application of AI in specialized education and training.

items.title: United by AI: An Interconnected Ecosystem of Appliances, Cars and Robots - 매일경제
items.summary: An article discusses the vision of an interconnected ecosystem where AI unites appliances, cars, and robots, showcasing broad applications of AI across various industries.

items.title: Structure and Implementation of New Practical English Textbooks Driven by Artificial Intelligence
items.summary: This paper explores the structure and implementation of new AI-driven practical English textbooks that use adaptive learning systems for diagnosis, task recommendation, and feedback.

items.title: A Prompt-Engineering Approach to Develop Scalable, Flexible, and Real-Time Hybrid Micro-Level Personalization in a General Purpose AI Teaching Assistant
items.summary: This study presents a prompt-engineering framework for personalizing general-purpose LLM/RAG-based AI teaching assistants, aiming for scalable, flexible, and real-time hybrid micro-level personalization.

items.title: AutoGraphForge: Towards Automated Graph Theory Discovery
items.summary: This project introduces AutoGraphForge, a computational pipeline for automated graph theory discovery, featuring a system for conjecturing, refuting, formalizing, and proving mathematical conjectures.

items.title: PPO-STGNN: A Proximal Policy Optimization Approach with Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for DAG Task Scheduling in Cloud-Edge-End Computing
items.summary: This research proposes PPO-STGNN, a Proximal Policy Optimization approach combined with Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks, for optimizing DAG task scheduling in complex cloud-edge-end computing environments.

items.title: Feature Reconfiguration With Visual Prior for Medical Lesion Segmentation
items.summary: This research proposes a method using feature reconfiguration with a visual prior to improve medical lesion segmentation, addressing challenges like complex background interference and diverse lesion morphology.

items.title: The Attention Triangle in Audio-Video Models
items.summary: This research probes and analyzes the 'attention triangle' in audio-video diffusion models, studying how cross-modal attention mechanisms can lead to semantic leakage.

items.title: A computable representation of the physical laboratory enables verifiable workflows
items.summary: This research establishes a computable representation of the physical laboratory using typed research objects and compositional workflows, enabling verifiable scientific processes.

items.title: Analysis of Prompt Engineering for Drug Toxicity Prediction
items.summary: This paper presents an analysis of prompt engineering as an AI application for predicting drug toxicity, aiming to reduce the high costs and failure rates in clinical trials.

items.title: Synthetic Semantic Supervision for Contrastive Code Representation Learning in Small Transformers: An Empirical Study
items.summary: This empirical study investigates Synthetic Semantic Supervision for contrastive code representation learning in small transformers, addressing challenges in generating general-purpose code embeddings.

items.title: Transfiver: Human-AI Co-Inference through a Shared Editable State
items.summary: This item introduces Transfiver, a transparent framework for interactive, verifiable, and editable representation, facilitating long-term human-AI co-inference through a shared editable state.

items.title: Govern the Model, Not Only the Data: Storage, Circulation, and Learning in Creative AI
items.summary: This discusses the concept of governing AI models, not just data, focusing on storage, circulation, and learning mechanisms like federated learning within creative AI contexts.

items.title: Semantic Bayesian World Models
items.summary: This paper proposes Semantic Bayesian World Models, an approach to integrate knowledge graphs with foundation models and autonomous agents by aligning crisp assertions with probabilistic reasoning.

items.title: Adapting to Evolving Requirements: Agentic AI for Retail Supply Chain Operations
items.summary: This research explores the application of Agentic AI for adapting to evolving requirements in retail supply chain operations, extending LLMs beyond individual optimization models.

items.title: Bioinfoysis Technical Report
items.summary: This technical report discusses the application of large language model agents in bioinformatics, highlighting challenges in long-horizon tasks that require planning and tool use.

items.title: More Criticism Does Not Make a Better Review: EquiReview-R
items.summary: This paper investigates the quality of reviews generated by AI, arguing that more criticism does not equate to a better review. It identifies issues like missing consequential weaknesses or making unsupported allegations, suggesting these failures require specific corrections beyond simple generation.

items.title: FiMI Banking: A Sovereign Model for Indian Retail Banking
items.summary: This paper introduces "FiMI Banking," a sovereign model designed to meet the specific operational and regulatory requirements for conversational systems in Indian retail banking. It addresses the shortcomings of general-purpose language models in handling complex, industry-specific tasks.

items.title: The Dually Flat Geometry of Planning as Inference
items.summary: This paper presents a novel characterization of the occupancy measure in reinforcement learning, achieved by embedding the planning criterion into dynamics via a resetting process. It introduces a "visitation measure" derived from this approach, grounded in information geometry.

items.title: LLM4CKD: Large Language Models for Early Stage Chronic Kidney Disease Screening
items.summary: This study, titled "LLM4CKD," evaluates the effectiveness of Large Language Models for early-stage Chronic Kidney Disease screening. It aims to overcome limitations of traditional ML/DL methods that require extensive labeled data and model training for real-world application.

items.title: InSituMeasure: Probing Situated Measurement Grounding in Industrial Scenes with Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper, "InSituMeasure," probes the effectiveness of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in performing situated measurement grounding, such as reading industrial gauges. It finds MLLMs unreliable for continuous-valued measurements in industrial scenes, despite their strong performance on general multimodal benchmarks.

items.title: Instruction Duplication as an Inference-Time Control Primitive
items.summary: This paper introduces "instruction duplication," a minimal black-box inference-time control primitive designed to improve procedural instruction following in language-model systems. It aims to enhance control, especially when generated trajectories are subsequently inspected or repaired.

items.title: IRWOZ 2.0: A Large Language Model-driven Dialogue Dataset for Industrial Robot Conversations
items.summary: This paper introduces "IRWOZ 2.0," an updated Large Language Model-driven dialogue dataset specifically designed for industrial robot conversations. This new version addresses significant noise issues in dialogue states and utterances present in the original IRWOZ, improving state-tracking accuracy for human-robot interaction systems.

items.title: Spurious Advantage Hidden in GRPO
items.summary: This research reveals a "spurious advantage" within Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a method for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. It explains how GRPO's advantage estimator can assign magnitudes to rollouts based on within-group reward statistics in a potentially misleading way.

items.title: Why Gated DeltaNet Survives 4-Bit Quantization: NVFP4 W4A4 for the Recurrent Half of a Hybrid 27B LLM
items.summary: This research investigates why Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers within hybrid 27B LLMs are robust to 4-bit quantization, specifically using NVFP4 W4A4 for the recurrent half. It analyzes how this allows for efficient quantization of models like Qwen3.8-27B.

items.title: The Geometry of Ignorance: LLMs Know When to Temper Bayesian Priors
items.summary: This research, "The Geometry of Ignorance," investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) handle uncertainty, revealing that their unembedding geometry encodes Bayesian priors. This mechanism allows the model to fall back on the unigram distribution of its training corpus when it has few clues.

items.title: Equation Recast for Canonical Operator Learning Across Parametric PDEs
items.summary: This paper introduces a novel method called "Equation Recast" for Canonical Operator Learning across Parametric Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). It aims to improve learning solution operators over broad parameter ranges for data-driven models, particularly addressing failures outside the training distribution.

items.title: From Euclidean to Graph-Structured Data: A Survey of Collaborative Learning
items.summary: This paper presents a survey of "Collaborative Learning," transitioning from Euclidean to graph-structured data. It explores how this approach addresses fundamental limitations of conventional machine learning, such as scalability and privacy.

items.title: Modern Transformers Are Implicit Hybrids: From Functional Differentiation to Principled Hybrid Architecture Design
items.summary: This research argues that modern Transformers are implicitly hybrid architectures, combining full and linear attention mechanisms. It seeks an evidence-grounded basis for principled hybrid architecture design by analyzing the head-level functional organization learned by RoPE-based Transformers.

items.title: Tail-Likelihood Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces "Tail-Likelihood Reinforcement Learning," a new approach that addresses limitations of optimizing average reward in generative policies. It focuses on distinguishing policies that might yield the same mean reward but have different probabilities of producing rare, high-reward rollouts.

items.title: Mesh-Native Physics-Informed Graph Surrogates for TCAD-in-the-Loop Design Space Exploration
items.summary: This paper proposes mesh-native physics-informed graph surrogates to enable more efficient design space exploration for FinFET devices, addressing the computational expense of traditional TCAD simulations.

items.title: TRACE: Spatiotemporal Contact Memory Graph Network Simulator for Granular Dynamics
items.summary: This research introduces TRACE, a spatiotemporal contact memory graph network simulator designed to efficiently model granular dynamics by better preserving inter-granular contact history.

items.title: Evaluating Graph Neural Networks for Change-Criticality Classification in Maritime Navigation Charts
items.summary: This study evaluates the effectiveness of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for classifying change-criticality in maritime navigation charts, investigating optimal message-passing operations and architectural configurations.

items.title: Causal Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper proposes 'Causal Foundation Models' as a novel approach to causal inference, aiming to generalize across diverse problems without requiring a bespoke pipeline for each new application.

items.title: Learnable composition for neural operators
items.summary: This work explores learnable composition for neural operators to improve their accuracy and generalization when applied to physical simulations with varying domain geometries or operating conditions.

items.title: LeanStream: A Speculate-and-Refine Streaming Framework for Efficient on-Device LLM Inference
items.summary: LeanStream is presented as a speculate-and-refine streaming framework designed for efficient on-device LLM inference, particularly on mobile and embedded devices with limited DRAM.

items.title: The Gradient Does Not See Rank: Rank-Indifference in Matrix-CODI on ProsQA
items.summary: This research investigates 'rank-indifference' in Matrix-CODI, a type of continuous chain-of-thought model, analyzing how gradients perceive the structural observable of latent matrices.

items.title: Distilling deep optical flow stereo methods to retrieve dense three-dimensional wind fields
items.summary: This paper describes a method for distilling deep optical flow stereo techniques to accurately retrieve dense three-dimensional wind fields from geostationary atmospheric motion vectors.

items.title: Scaling Laws, Tabular Data and Actuarial Ratemaking Models
items.summary: This study investigates whether scaling laws observed in deep learning models also apply to actuarial ratemaking models, which utilize tabular, heterogeneous, and noisy data.

items.title: Kernel Reboot: Breaking the Boundaries of Neural Tangent Kernels for Neural Fields
items.summary: This research explores how to extend Neural Tangent Kernels (NTK) to improve fast, high-quality reconstruction of neural fields from sparse observations, addressing NTK's linear limitations.

items.title: Routing Is Not Enough: Diagnosing Intra-Adapter Subspace Contention in MoE+LoRA Fine-Tuning
items.summary: This paper diagnoses intra-adapter subspace contention in MoE+LoRA fine-tuning for multi-domain applications, testing the assumption that token-level routing effectively separates domain-specific updates.

items.title: Frontier LLMs are effective batch optimizers: Assessing reasoning models in continuous and discrete settings
items.summary: This study assesses the effectiveness of frontier large language models (LLMs) as batch optimizers in both continuous and discrete settings, highlighting their potential for optimization tasks.

items.title: Language-encoded network topology enables large language models to reason about complex networks
items.summary: This research proposes a method where language-encoded network topology enables large language models to effectively reason about and understand the structure of complex networks.

items.title: FlowBalance: Verifier-Grounded Self-Improvement from On-Policy Reasoning Experience
items.summary: FlowBalance is introduced as a method for verifier-grounded self-improvement in reasoning models, allowing them to learn from on-policy experience while mitigating risks of false confidence.

items.title: Geometry-Aware Graph Construction via Adaptive Spectral Bandwidth Control
items.summary: This paper presents geometry-aware graph construction via adaptive spectral bandwidth control, improving kernelized graph methods by optimizing Gaussian bandwidth for local kernel operators.

items.title: Risk and Anomaly Identification for Distribution Network Optimal Operation Based on Reinforcement Learning and Uncertainty Quantification
items.summary: This research proposes a method for risk and anomaly identification in distribution network operations, leveraging reinforcement learning and uncertainty quantification for improved reliability.

items.title: DE-Venus: A Data-Efficient RLVR Framework for Large Language Models
items.summary: DE-Venus is a data-efficient RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards) framework designed to improve the practical scalability of large language model reasoning by addressing cost and data constraints.

items.title: A Large Open Multi-Energy Corpus of Soil Compaction Tests, with Machine-Learning Baselines
items.summary: This paper introduces a large, open corpus of soil compaction test data along with machine learning baselines, facilitating research into soil property predictions for engineered fills.

items.title: Gradients Know What Outcomes Don't: Unlocking Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning with Gradient-Aligned Rewards
items.summary: This research paper proposes a new method called Gradient-Aligned Rewards to improve reinforcement learning for chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models by providing more nuanced feedback than binary outcomes.

items.title: From Zero to Hero: An Open LLM Ecosystem for Armenian
items.summary: This paper addresses the scarcity of resources for Armenian LLMs by curating and releasing two datasets and the necessary recipe to reproduce an open LLM ecosystem for this low-resource language.

items.title: SimpleDesign: A Joint Model for Protein Sequence and Structure Codesign
items.summary: This paper presents SimpleDesign, a joint model developed for the codesign of protein sequences and their three-dimensional structures, crucial for understanding biological processes.

items.title: Inferred Generative-Process Diversity Predicts Correlated Failure Across Language Models
items.summary: This research investigates how diversity in generative processes can predict correlated failure modes across multiple language models, analyzing the resilience of collective AI systems.

items.title: TraveL: Transformer-based Multi-view Path Distributional Representation Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces TraveL, a Transformer-based method for multi-view path distributional representation learning, aiming to improve how road networks are understood and analyzed for various applications.

items.title: It's the Problem, Not the Path: Budget and Difficulty Confounds in LLM Reasoning Trajectories
items.summary: This paper analyzes confounding factors like budget and difficulty in large language model reasoning trajectories, providing controls to better understand when and why breakthroughs or failures occur.

items.title: Beyond Straightness: Non-Crossing Flow Matching via Quantile AlignTree Coupling
items.summary: This paper presents a new method, Non-Crossing Flow Matching via Quantile AlignTree Coupling, to enhance the performance of Flow Matching by creating higher quality, non-crossing couplings between distributions.

items.title: A Two-Stage Forecasting System for CPU Workload Prediction in Private Clouds
items.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage forecasting system designed to accurately predict CPU workload in private cloud environments, which is essential for optimizing resource provisioning and maintaining QoS.

items.title: An Adversarial Zero-Shot Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Multivariate IoT Traffic Data
items.summary: This paper proposes a novel framework utilizing an adversarial zero-shot learning approach for anomaly detection in multivariate IoT traffic data, addressing challenges like device diversity and lack of labeled data.

items.title: LeanGRPO: Eliminating Redundant Recomputation in Diffusion RL
items.summary: This paper introduces LeanGRPO, a method to improve the efficiency of Diffusion Reinforcement Learning by eliminating redundant recomputation steps during on-policy training.

items.title: Neural-Network Maxent: a general extension with learned nonlinearity, applied to time-series for Desert Locust distribution modelling
items.summary: This paper presents Neural-Network Maxent, an extension of the Maxent method with learned nonlinearity, applied to time-series data for modeling the distribution of the Desert Locust.

items.title: On the Interaction Between Model Compression and Test-Time Adaptation
items.summary: This research systematically analyzes the interaction between model compression and test-time adaptation, exploring how structured compression affects the adaptability of deep neural networks.

items.title: Local Updates, Global Learning (LUGL): Playing Games with non-incremental Learners
items.summary: This paper proposes Local Updates, Global Learning (LUGL), a new approach for playing games with non-incremental learners in reinforcement learning, addressing challenges in self-play training.

items.title: Out-of-Distribution Generalisation with Sequence Models in Offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper presents a principled analysis and empirical investigation into out-of-distribution generalization for sequence models in offline multi-agent reinforcement learning, aiming to improve zero-shot task generalization.

items.title: Projected Riemannian Gradient Descent for the Bures-Wasserstein Barycenter: Dimension-Independent Linear Convergence at Unit Step Size
items.summary: This paper introduces a projected Riemannian gradient descent method for computing the Bures-Wasserstein barycenter, an optimization problem relevant to machine learning and quantum information. It demonstrates dimension-independent linear convergence at unit step size.

items.title: Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection
items.summary: This research investigates the generalization performance of linear probes used to detect behaviors and concepts within large language model activations, specifically for out-of-distribution deception detection using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It suggests that probe generalization can be viewed as subspace selection.

items.title: PiPMRE: A Pipeline Based on Language Model for Medical Relation Extraction
items.summary: This paper proposes PiPMRE, a language model-based pipeline for medical relation extraction (MRE) that jointly extracts entities and their relations from medical text. It addresses challenges found in previous MRE approaches that treat the task as sequence tagging.

items.title: Margins, Not Windows: Training-Free Per-Step Lossy Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This research introduces a training-free, per-step lossy speculative decoding method for accelerating LLM inference, focusing on using 'margins' instead of fixed 'windows.' It aims to improve efficiency by drafting and verifying candidate tokens in parallel, going beyond traditional strict token-matching rules.

items.title: Distilled Rapid Embedding Transfer (DRET): Parameter-Efficient Biomedical Domain Adaptation via Priority-Based Embedding Transfer
items.summary: This paper introduces Distilled Rapid Embedding Transfer (DRET), a parameter-efficient method for biomedical domain adaptation of language models. It leverages priority-based embedding transfer to enable lightweight general-purpose models to perform well on domain-specific NLP tasks.

items.title: Unifying Conformal Language Tasks with In-Context Ensembles
items.summary: This paper proposes unifying various conformal language tasks, such as summarization and extractive question answering, using in-context ensembles. It focuses on effectively retrieving relevant content under constraints of coverage and conciseness.

items.title: Large Language Models in Resolving Contextual Knowledge Conflicts
items.summary: This research investigates how Large Language Models resolve conflicts that arise within contextual knowledge, distinguishing them from conflicts between parametric and external knowledge. It introduces a taxonomy of six types of contextual conflicts.

items.title: LLMs Learn Better In-Context from Rules than from Examples
items.summary: This research paper compares the effectiveness of in-context learning in LLMs, finding that models learn better from rules (instruction following) than from examples.

items.title: SWIM: Student Writing Simulation via Proficiency-Conditioned Generation
items.summary: Introduces SWIM, a method for simulating student writing proficiency using LLMs, exploring how models can reproduce varied writing styles and content.

items.title: What Else Needs Fixing? Exploring Cost-Effective Test-Time Compute for Revision Propagation in Artifacts Generated Through Conversation
items.summary: Explores methods for cost-effective test-time compute to propagate revisions in artifacts generated by LLMs through conversational interactions.

items.title: Contextual Tamil Spelling and Grammar Correction Using Progressively Fine-Tuned Sequence-to-Sequence Transformers
items.summary: Presents a method for contextual Tamil spelling and grammar correction using progressively fine-tuned sequence-to-sequence transformers, addressing challenges in a low-resource language.

items.title: How Perturbations Propagate: A Multi-Level Analysis of Robustness in Large Language Models
items.summary: This research analyzes how various input perturbations, such as typos and corrupted text, propagate through decoder-only language models, affecting their robustness.

items.title: TabScope: Question-Adaptive Scope Selection for Table Question Answering
items.summary: Introduces TabScope, a method for question-adaptive scope selection to improve Large Language Models' accuracy in table question answering, especially with larger tables.

items.title: Decoupled Analysis-Judging: An Automated Creativity Evaluator Using LLMs in Complex Multi-step Creativity Tasks
items.summary: Presents Decoupled Analysis-Judging, an automated creativity evaluator that uses LLMs in complex multi-step tasks, addressing challenges like verbosity and leniency biases.

items.title: Pattern Over-Generalization of Knowledge Graph Embedding
items.summary: This research paper analyzes the problem of pattern over-generalization in knowledge graph embedding (KGE) models, which can hinder their effectiveness in predicting missing links by miscapturing inference patterns.

items.title: Lost in Reordering: Structural Sensitivity of Multilingual LLMs under Semantics-Preserving Perturbations
items.summary: This research investigates the structural sensitivity of multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) to semantics-preserving perturbations, particularly in free word-order languages, highlighting an underexplored aspect of their robustness.

items.title: The Impact of Synthetic Data Augmentation on Discourse-Pragmatic Function Classification
items.summary: This paper investigates the impact of synthetic data augmentation on discourse-pragmatic function classification in NLP, focusing on the geometric relationship between generated and real training data rather than just quantity.

items.title: A Circuit for Plural Reference: How LLMs Represent and Retrieve Singular and Plural Entities
items.summary: This research investigates the internal mechanisms and "circuits" within Large Language Models (LLMs) for representing and retrieving singular and plural entities to handle plural reference, using mechanistic interpretability and attention analysis.

items.title: Typological Feature Prediction with Large Language Models: An In-Context Learning Approach
items.summary: This research explores an in-context learning approach for typological feature prediction using Large Language Models, aiming to provide more interpretable justifications and improve performance in multilingual NLP.

items.title: Evaluating Criterion-Conditioned Behaviour of Large Language Models in Content Moderation
items.summary: This research evaluates the criterion-conditioned behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs) in content moderation, examining their ability to disentangle and reliably apply multiple moderation criteria rather than aggregated labels.

items.title: Exemplar: Classical Priors Complement Frozen Features for Few-Shot Microscopy Segmentation at Native Resolution
items.summary: This paper introduces Exemplar, a few-shot segmenter for microscopy segmentation that combines a frozen DINOv3 backbone with classical native-resolution filter responses to effectively process new biomedical datasets.

items.title: Solving the Needle-in-a-Haystack Problem in Mammography Vision-Language Model with Differentiable Subset Sampling
items.summary: This research explores a new method called Differentiable Subset Sampling to solve the 'needle-in-a-haystack problem' in mammography Vision-Language Models, improving their zero-shot performance in clinical tasks like cancer detection.

items.title: WireSeg-32K: A Physics-Grounded Synthetic Dataset for Wire Instance Segmentation
items.summary: This paper introduces WireSeg-32K, a physics-grounded synthetic dataset designed for instance segmentation of deformable linear objects like wires and cables, addressing challenges in obtaining large-scale real-world annotations.

items.title: Who Speaks for the Pruned? Visual Token Pruning as Coverage Optimization
items.summary: This paper proposes CoverPruner, a training-free method for visual token pruning in vision-language models (VLMs) that optimizes coverage to reduce inference costs more effectively than traditional methods.

items.title: Learning to Zoom Efficiently with a Contrastive Curriculum
items.summary: This research demonstrates a novel contrastive curriculum approach to efficiently teach visual agents to use zoom-in tools for high-resolution images, reducing the need for extensive supervised fine-tuning.

items.title: Counting Animals in Camera-Traps Image Sequences without Count Labels: Winning Solution to the iWildCam 2021 Challenge
items.summary: This winning solution to the iWildCam 2021 Challenge describes a computer vision method for counting animals in camera-trap image sequences without requiring count labels, aiding wildlife monitoring.

items.title: An Ensemble-Based Self-Taught Learning Approach for Parking Space Classification Under Limited Data
items.summary: This study investigates an ensemble-based self-taught learning approach for parking space classification, aiming to improve generalization and overcome limitations of deep learning under limited annotated data.

items.title: Tensor-based Brain Surface Modeling and Analysis
items.summary: This research presents a unified computational approach for tensor-based morphometry, enabling the detection and analysis of brain surface shape differences between clinical groups using magnetic resonance images.

items.title: When Depth Hurts: Reliability-Aware Geometry Distillation for Depth-Free RGB-D Salient Object Detection
items.summary: This work introduces Reliability-Aware Geometry Distillation for Depth-Free RGB-D Salient Object Detection, addressing how unreliable depth data can degrade multimodal fusion in SOD models.

items.title: FoRIS: Progressive Foreground Refinement for Training-Free In-Context Segmentation
items.summary: FoRIS proposes Progressive Foreground Refinement for training-free In-Context Segmentation (ICS), viewing it as a coarse-to-fine process to precisely segment arbitrary semantic concepts from visual exemplars.

items.title: Exploring the Potential of Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data
items.summary: This research explores extending Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) to multi-source remote sensing data, including SAR, to better leverage heterogeneous sensor information for vision-language understanding.

items.title: Neural-Collapse-guided Task-Free Continual Anomaly Detection
items.summary: This paper introduces a Neural-Collapse-guided Task-Free Continual Anomaly Detection method for industrial visual inspection, addressing the challenge of unpredictable data shifts in real-world manufacturing environments.

items.title: When Do Frozen VLMs Respond to Image-Free Object-Token Edits? An Answer-Key-Free Protocol and What It Reveals
items.summary: This research presents an 'answer-key-free protocol' to investigate how frozen Vision-Language Models (VLMs) respond to image-free object-token edits at the representation level for answering 'what-if' queries about a scene.

items.title: BMCTrack-d: Pig re-identification and tracking via back marks in challenging camera settings
items.summary: This research introduces BMCTrack-d, a system for individual pig re-identification and long-term tracking using back marks in challenging camera settings, essential for automated animal health and welfare monitoring.

items.title: Tree species mapping in Denmark: A comparison of spectral-temporal features with geospatial foundation model embeddings
items.summary: This study maps tree species across Denmark using National Forest Inventory plots and Earth Observation data, evaluating the potential of foundation models and spectral-temporal features for large-scale forest characterization.

items.title: Residual Optimal Transport-Based Experts Collaboration Towards Modality-Aware Infrared-Visible Object Detection
items.summary: This paper proposes a Residual Optimal Transport-Based Experts Collaboration method for modality-aware infrared-visible object detection, addressing challenges where sensor modalities may be intermittently unavailable.

items.title: Neural Video Compression Based on Deformable Temporal Alignment and Difference-aware Fusion
items.summary: This research presents a neural video compression technique based on deformable temporal alignment and difference-aware fusion to improve performance by addressing motion estimation and alignment errors in propagated context.

items.title: WIDE: Wildcard Inference with Dynamic Expansion for Cross-Modal Generative Retrieval
items.summary: WIDE proposes a novel approach for wildcard inference with dynamic expansion, designed to overcome information asymmetry challenges in cross-modal generative retrieval tasks.

items.title: Building Pretraining Data for World Models: An Unreal Engine-Based Pipeline for Action-Conditioned Video Generation
items.summary: This paper describes an Unreal Engine-based pipeline for generating large-scale, action-conditioned video data, specifically designed for pretraining world models to support video generation.

items.title: Occlusion-Robust Multimodal Emotion Recognition in VR via Fusion of Facial Images and EMG
items.summary: This research develops a method for occlusion-robust multimodal emotion recognition in VR by fusing facial images and electromyography (EMG) data, addressing limitations posed by head-mounted displays.

items.title: PL-SCEA: Reconfiguring Pretrained Attention for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection
items.summary: PL-SCEA proposes reconfiguring pretrained attention in Vision Foundation Models to enhance few-shot industrial anomaly detection, addressing the mismatch between pretraining objectives and anomaly detection needs.

items.title: ARCOS: Zero-shot Boundary Localization for Corneal Layer Segmentation Across Optical Coherence Tomography Devices
items.summary: ARCOS proposes a zero-shot boundary localization method for accurate corneal layer segmentation in Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) devices, crucial for assessing corneal morphology in healthcare.

items.title: CoFiE: Coarse-to-Fine Evidence Selection for Efficient Streaming Video Understanding
items.summary: This paper presents CoFiE, a method for coarse-to-fine evidence selection to improve the efficiency of Vision Language Models (VLLMs) in streaming video understanding. It focuses on reducing visual tokens after encoding to meet tight latency constraints for user queries.

items.title: Understanding Autonomous Driving Datasets by Describing Differences between Image Subsets in Natural Language
items.summary: This research explores methods to understand large-scale autonomous driving datasets by describing differences between image subsets in natural language. This understanding is crucial for ensuring safety and robustness of autonomous systems by identifying issues like domain shift.

items.title: DropClick: Semi-Automated One-Click Segmentation for Agricultural Robotic Data
items.summary: This paper introduces DropClick, a semi-automated, click-guided segmentation tool designed to simplify the laborious process of labeling vision datasets for agricultural robotics. It aims to accelerate novel developments by making segmentation annotation more efficient.

items.title: ToPO: Token-Conditioned Preference Routing for Attention-Based Latent Diffusion Models
items.summary: This paper proposes ToPO (Token-Oriented Preference Optimization), a new method for attention-based latent diffusion models using token-conditioned preference routing. ToPO constructs a separable spatial-temporal mechanism per minibatch for noise-prediction models.

items.title: Semantic-Aware Subgraph State Space Model for WSI Classification in Histopathology
items.summary: This research presents a Semantic-Aware Subgraph State Space Model for Whole Slide Image (WSI) classification in histopathology. The method focuses on recognizing characteristic histological patterns, including spatial distribution and co-occurrence of structures, for subtyping.

items.title: Observation-Conditioned Latent Energy Priors for Sparse Implicit Neural Shape Completion
items.summary: This paper explores Observation-Conditioned Latent Energy Priors for Sparse Implicit Neural Shape Completion. It focuses on optimizing latent codes from sparse samples when using implicit neural representations for 3D shape modeling.

items.title: SignSeek: Learning Transferable Representations for Sign Dictionary Retrieval
items.summary: This research presents SignSeek, a method for learning transferable representations to enable automatic sign dictionary retrieval from query videos. It addresses the challenge of variability between signers in sign language recognition.

items.title: GPU-Accelerated Astrodynamics World Models for Spacecraft Rendezvous and Proximity Operations
items.summary: This paper explores GPU-Accelerated Astrodynamics World Models for spacecraft rendezvous and proximity operations. These world models enable multi-step planning and trajectory prediction by learning state-action dynamics and observation models from offline data.

items.title: Sensing Which Modality Matters: Evidence-Gated Regularization for Robust VLA Policies
items.summary: This research introduces Evidence-Gated Regularization for Robust Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Policies, addressing the issue of modality entanglement during training. The method aims to improve the robustness of VLA policies under real-world occlusions and distractors.

items.title: Following a Unique Path: A Fast Certifier Applied to Outlier-Robust Pose Registration
items.summary: This paper presents a Fast Certifier for Outlier-Robust Pose Registration, using certifiable methods to guarantee global optimality for non-convex problems. It utilizes convex semidefinite programming relaxations to verify solutions obtained from local solvers.

items.title: TRaIL-Odom: Tightly Coupled Continuous Time Radar-IMU-LiDAR Odometry with Adaptive Doppler Weighting
items.summary: This paper presents TRaIL-Odom, a novel method for tightly coupled continuous-time Radar-IMU-LiDAR odometry that adaptively weights Doppler information, addressing limitations of fixed residual weights in existing sensor fusion techniques.

items.title: WISE: World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: This paper presents WISE (World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling), a method for efficient post-training of Vision-Language-Action models by leveraging world models to evaluate candidate behaviors through imagined futures, reducing reliance on costly real-world exploration.

items.title: Catalogue Photography as a Cold Start: Toward Deployable Carbide Burr Recognition
items.summary: This paper presents a computer vision method for quality assurance in manufacturing, specifically for recognizing carbide burrs, by addressing a cold-start problem with limited labeled imagery.

items.title: Subspace Inference Enables Efficient Active Reward Learning from Preferences
items.summary: This paper proposes a method called Subspace Inference to make Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) more sample-efficient for learning reward models by synthesizing informative preference queries.

items.title: Learning 3D Editing without Paired Supervision via Generative Prior Distillation

items.title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
items.summary: This research introduces Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization (MCPO) for compressing Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) in large reasoning models. The aim is to reduce computational costs and KV-cache pressure from long reasoning trajectories.

items.title: VICAL: Vicinal Consistency Alignment for Long-Tailed Visual Recognition

items.title: MINT: A Unified Model for World-Space Camera and Hand Motion Estimation from Scalable Egocentric Pipeline Supervision
items.summary: This research presents MINT, a unified model designed for world-space camera and hand motion estimation from egocentric video. This capability is crucial for activity understanding, robot learning, and augmented reality applications.

items.title: ARC-Loc: Leveraging Azimuthal Ray Convergence as a Geometric Cue for Direct Cross-View Localization
items.summary: This paper introduces ARC-Loc, a method that leverages azimuthal ray convergence as a geometric cue for direct cross-view localization. It aims to estimate the pose of a ground image by matching it to a geo-referenced satellite image.

items.title: RefDiT: Local Attribute Guidance in Reference-Based Image Generation
items.summary: This research introduces RefDiT, a method for local attribute guidance in reference-based image generation. It aims to improve personalization models and style transfer by generating new images guided by subject references.

items.summary: This research explores the use of compositional reward models for conditional medical image generation, particularly with diffusion models like ControlNet. The goal is to generate high-quality medical images conditioned on semantic masks, reducing annotation costs.

items.title: FailureSpot: Label-Efficient Timestamp-Level Failure Detection for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: This research introduces FailureSpot, a label-efficient method for timestamp-level failure detection in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. This is essential for the safe and reliable deployment of general-purpose robotic manipulation systems.

items.title: VLA-Precision: Asymmetric Co-Bootstrapping for Efficient Real-World Online RL of Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: This paper presents VLA-Precision, a method using asymmetric co-bootstrapping and real-world online reinforcement learning to improve the precision of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. This enhances their reliability for tasks demanding precision in robotic manipulation.

items.title: SocioGesture: Real-Time and Adaptive Social Gesture Perception for Human-Robot Interaction
items.summary: This paper introduces SocioGesture, a real-time and adaptive system for social gesture perception in human-robot interaction. It enables robots to infer social cues like invitations and refusals from noisy onboard perception for better interaction.

items.title: Continual Field-Adaptive Models (CFAMs) for Post-Deployment Physical AI
items.summary: This research proposes Continual Field-Adaptive Models (CFAMs) for post-deployment physical AI, aiming to achieve unattended interactive autonomy. These models enable deployed systems, like robots, to adapt to novelty in mission-critical operations with scarce training data.

items.title: Open-Set 3D Scene Graphs for Field Robotics: An Outdoor Case Study
items.summary: This paper investigates Open-Set 3D Scene Graphs (3DSGs) for field robotics, focusing on their behavior in real-world outdoor deployments. These graphs aim to provide geometrically grounded and semantically informed maps to support high-level robotic reasoning.

items.title: Dressing in Motion: A Human Motion-Aware Diffusion Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing
items.summary: This research proposes a human motion-aware diffusion policy for robot-assisted dressing, aiming to help older adults with physical impairments. The policy enables robots to generate actions aligned with human arm movements despite complex garment-human contact and occlusions.

items.title: HaptiNet: Networked Haptic Robots Enable Physical Co-presence in Geographically-Unconstrained Rehabilitation
items.summary: This paper introduces HaptiNet, a system of networked haptic robots designed to enable physical co-presence for cooperative rehabilitation, allowing users to transmit forces and coordinate movements remotely.

items.title: Coupled Control and Wireless World Models for Resilient Remote Robotic Control
items.summary: This paper explores coupled control and wireless world models to achieve resilient remote robotic control, addressing challenges like limited communication resources and environmental disturbances when operating over wireless networks.

items.title: Reasoning Without Inference Cost: Latent Semantic Scaffolding for Robot VLA Policies
items.summary: This research introduces latent semantic scaffolding to enable causal reasoning in robot Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies without incurring inference costs, aiming to improve manipulation capabilities.

items.title: A Schema Bounded Language Model for Refining Robot Policies Without Destabilizing Local Learning
items.summary: This paper explores using schema-bounded language models to refine navigation policies for composite heterogeneous robots in decentralized systems, ensuring stable local learning while leveraging different LLM backends.

items.title: LIBERO-RECOVER: Beyond Task Success Towards Failure Recovery in Robotic Manipulation Models
items.summary: This research introduces LIBERO-RECOVER to address failure recovery in robotic manipulation models, aiming to move beyond simple task success metrics for more robust real-world deployment of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.

items.title: Morphology and actuation as inductive biases in robotic hand manipulation
items.summary: This paper analyzes the influence of morphology and actuation as inductive biases in robotic hand manipulation, examining how structural choices impact joint coordination and system control complexity.

items.title: TacPAC: Tactile Prediction and Real-Time Action Correction in World-Action Models for Contact-Rich Manipulation
items.summary: This paper presents TacPAC, which integrates tactile prediction and real-time action correction into world-action models to enhance contact-rich robotic manipulation by providing crucial local contact cues.

items.title: Temporal Tactile Encoding and Compliance for Intent-Aware Robot-to-Human Bimanual Handover
items.summary: This research focuses on intent-aware robot-to-human bimanual handover, using temporal tactile encoding and compliance to allow robots to infer when a person is ready to receive an object and release it safely.

items.title: Human-Human & Human-Robot Interaction Transformer (H2INT) for Robot Navigation in Dense and Uncertain Crowds
items.summary: This paper introduces H2INT, a Human-Human & Human-Robot Interaction Transformer, to improve robot navigation in dense and uncertain crowds by enabling robots to reason about and respond to pedestrian motion.

items.title: RoboSPA: Can VLA Models Go Beyond Simple Scenes and Short-Horizon Tasks?
items.summary: This research, RoboSPA, investigates whether Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can extend their robotic manipulation capabilities beyond simple scenes and short-horizon tasks, examining their reasoning under increasing spatial and procedural complexity.

items.title: Adaptation Needs in Robotic Systems: Assessing Behavior Trees and Their Enhancement
items.summary: This research assesses Behavior Trees (BTs) and their enhancement to address adaptation needs in robotic systems operating in dynamic, uncertain, and open-ended environments, improving effective and safe operation.

items.title: Development of a Humanoid Robot Prototype for Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction
items.summary: This paper details the development of a humanoid robot prototype serving as a flexible testbed for integrating AI modules to facilitate multimodal human-robot interaction and intuitive collaboration.

items.title: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Procedural Reasoning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
items.summary: This research investigates a neuro-symbolic framework to enable long-horizon Vision-Language-Action (VLA) manipulation in robots, combining learned VLA control with symbolic reasoning for complex procedural tasks.

items.title: What Matters, When? Diagnosing and Improving Conditional Visual Grounding in Visuomotor Imitation Policies
items.summary: This paper diagnoses and aims to improve conditional visual grounding in visuomotor imitation policies, addressing how the visual target for successful control changes to enhance robotic manipulation in varied visual conditions.

items.title: Same Trajectory, Contradictory Rewards (ROBORMBENCH): Paraphrase Fragility in Vision Language Reward Models
items.summary: This research, ROBORMBENCH, exposes paraphrase fragility in Vision-Language Reward Models used for robotic learning, showing that semantically equivalent goal descriptions can lead to contradictory rewards for the same trajectory.

items.title: Toward Context-Aware Exoskeleton Assistance: Integrating Computer Vision Payload Estimation with a Multi-Metric Optimization Space
items.summary: This research aims for context-aware exoskeleton assistance by integrating computer vision for payload estimation with a multi-metric optimization framework, enabling a predictive adaptive control strategy for back-support exoskeletons.

items.title: A Biomimetic Vertebraic Soft Robotic Tail for High-Speed, High-Force Dynamic Maneuvering
items.summary: This research introduces a biomimetic vertebral soft robotic tail designed to enhance the stability and maneuverability of mobile robots, addressing the trade-off between power and safety in existing designs.

items.title: CoFreeVLA: Short-Horizon Collision-Free Dual-Arm Manipulation via Vision-Language-Action Model and Risk Estimation
items.summary: CoFreeVLA is proposed for short-horizon collision-free dual-arm manipulation, using a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model and risk estimation to overcome self-collision constraints in robotic deployments.

items.title: Squint: Fast Visual Reinforcement Learning for Sim-to-Real Robotics
items.summary: Squint presents a method for fast visual reinforcement learning specifically tailored for sim-to-real robotics, aiming to make the training process more efficient despite the inherent costs.

items.title: Persistent Robot World Models: Stabilizing Multi-Step Rollouts via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper explores persistent robot world models that generate future video frames for manipulated scenes, offering an alternative to traditional physics engines for simulating complex robotic tasks.

items.title: A Kinematic Framework for Screening Candidate Pinch Configurations in Robotic Hand Design without Object or Contact Models
items.summary: A kinematic framework is developed to screen candidate pinch configurations in robotic hand design, allowing evaluation of dexterity without relying on object or contact models in early design stages.

items.title: X2-N: A Transformable Wheel-legged Humanoid Robot with Dual-mode Locomotion and Manipulation
items.summary: X2-N is a transformable wheel-legged humanoid robot capable of dual-mode locomotion and manipulation, designed to efficiently traverse varied terrains by combining wheeled and legged system advantages.

items.summary: RedVLA introduces a physical red teaming methodology for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to proactively detect physical safety risks before their deployment in real-world robotic systems.

items.title: Predictive Zonotope Reduction: Precise Runtime Monitoring under Uncertainty
items.summary: This research introduces Predictive Zonotope Reduction, a method for precise runtime monitoring of robots operating in physical environments, enabling sound representation of uncertainty to ensure safety and prevent suboptimal actions.

items.summary: This paper introduces MINERVA (MINimal Efficient Robotic Vision-Action policy), a family of compact visuomotor policies, to investigate the minimum required capacity for Vision-Language-Action models to solve the LIBERO manipulation benchmark efficiently.

items.title: FWBC-VLA: Force-Aware Whole-Body Compensation for Contact-Rich Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: This paper introduces FWBC-VLA (Force-Aware Whole-Body Compensation for Contact-Rich Loco-Manipulation), a method that bridges Vision-Language-Action models with physical interaction control to enable robots to perform complex contact-rich locomotion and manipulation tasks.

items.title: Toward Unified Robot Learning: Bridging Representation, Vision-Language-Action, and World Models
items.summary: This paper presents a conceptual framework for unified robot learning, bridging representation learning, Vision-Language-Action models, and world models to enable robots to reliably perceive, act, and reason about actions in real-world environments.

items.summary: This paper introduces MulDP (Multimodal Diffusion Policy) for autonomous parkour navigation of quadruped robots across complex terrains, addressing challenges in fine-grained velocity regulation and high-level planning for agile locomotion.

items.title: Adaptive Vision-Language Grasping via Composable Foundation Priors and Generalizable Grasp Synthesis
items.summary: This paper proposes AdaRoboVLG, an adaptive Vision-Language-Grasp (VLG) framework for robots that enables generalizable grasp synthesis across different robotic hands by using composable foundation priors, distinguishing it from tightly coupled end-to-end VLG methods.

items.title: GIFT: Guided Intermediate Feature Training via Action-Oriented Structural Supervision for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: This paper introduces GIFT (Guided Intermediate Feature Training), a method that uses action-oriented structural supervision to enhance robot policies for manipulation by integrating richer semantic and dynamic visual features from vision-language pre-training and predictive world modeling.

items.title: Formation Matrix and Energy-based Control of Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: This paper describes an energy-based controller for a multi-agent robotic system, enabling it to achieve and maintain a specific formation on a plane while avoiding collisions between agents.

items.title: Dancing with REEM-C: A robot-to-human physical-social communication study
items.summary: This study investigates human-robot physical-social communication using the REEM-C robot to understand how robots can effectively convey information through physical interaction.

items.title: DogLegs: Robust Proprioceptive State Estimation for Legged Robots Using Multiple Leg-Mounted IMUs

items.title: SPARC: Spine with Prismatic And Revolute Compliance for Faster Quadrupedal Bounding

items.title: Vision-Based Tactile Sensing for the Perception of the Object's Compliance and Hardness

items.title: Static state was not enough for a long-running human-AI interaction
items.summary: Research suggests that static state mechanisms are insufficient for managing long-running interactions between humans and AI systems, implying a need for better memory.

items.title: Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents
items.summary: This paper introduces an environment-probing curation method for grounding agent memory in enterprise agents, aiming to prevent the preservation of errors or stale knowledge across sessions.

items.title: MOSAIC: Query-Aware Exploration Policy Adaptation for GraphRAG
items.summary: This paper introduces MOSAIC, a query-aware exploration policy adaptation method for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) systems to improve evidence connection across corpus graphs.

items.title: Memory Compression for High-Fanout Agent Sandboxes
items.summary: This paper addresses the memory bottleneck created by high-fanout agent sandboxes by proposing memory compression techniques that leverage shared templates and related trajectories across concurrent sessions.

items.title: PRAGMA: Evaluating Personalized Guidance with Memory Alignment in Lifelong Conversations
items.summary: This research introduces PRAGMA, a framework for evaluating personalized guidance with memory alignment in lifelong conversations with large language models. It addresses the challenges of inefficient and unreliable long interaction histories in personalized assistants.

items.title: Procedural Memory Under Change: Reuse and Interference in Controlled Web Tasks
items.summary: This study investigates procedural memory in language agents under changing conditions, focusing on the reuse and interference of successful routines in controlled web tasks. It examines how agents adapt when stored routines are no longer applicable.

items.title: Kernel-Managed Shared Memory for System-Wide Personalization
items.summary: This paper presents kernel-managed shared memory, a system-level abstraction designed for multi-agent AI systems to enable system-wide personalization by allowing specialized agents to share structured, tagged memory.

items.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs
items.summary: This research introduces Fortunate Recall, an ontology-driven memory lifecycle management system for LLMs, designed to maintain persistent coherence by strategically managing which memories persist, are replaced, and at what rate.

items.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
items.summary: Introduces ConvMem, a convolutional memory approach to extend the effective context window for Large Language Models by iteratively updating a fixed-size memory based on text segments. This method aims to improve long-context reasoning for LLMs.

items.title: REVA: Reusable Evidence View Aggregation for Context-Efficient RAG Serving
items.summary: This paper introduces REVA (Reusable Evidence View Aggregation), a method designed to improve context efficiency in RAG serving by compressing retrieved documents, thereby reducing latency and memory costs for knowledge-intensive LLM applications.

items.title: FlexComp: One Model for Every Ratio in Context Compression
items.summary: FlexComp introduces a soft context compression technique that condenses context into memory tokens, allowing one model to handle various compression ratios dynamically, unlike existing methods that require separately trained models for each ratio.

items.title: OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs
items.summary: Introduces "OmniKVQuant," a KV cache quantization method specifically for Omni-modal Large Language Models (Omni-LLMs) to reduce their high memory cost, adapting techniques previously used for text-only LLMs.

items.title: 2AM: Grounding Agent-Side Memory as Guidance for Steerable Action Models in Long-Horizon Manipulation
items.summary: This research explores grounding agent-side memory to provide guidance for steerable action models in long-horizon robot manipulation tasks, addressing challenges in combining VLAs with planners and geometric tools.

items.title: Memory as Plans: World-Action Modeling with Memory-Grounded Planning
items.summary: This paper explores 'Memory as Plans,' focusing on world-action modeling with memory-grounded planning to address long-horizon, non-Markovian manipulation tasks in robotics.

items.title: Video and image search in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base using Marengo 3.0
items.summary: TwelveLabs Marengo Embed 3.0 is now available as an embedding model in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, enabling natural language search for video, image, and audio content.

items.title: When Does Memory Help? A Cost-Aware Evaluation of Long-Term Memory in Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.summary: This paper introduces MERIT, a new evaluation framework for long-term memory in tool-using LLM agents, focusing on how remembered facts influence agent actions rather than just conversational recall.

items.title: EdgeMem: LLM-Free Agent Memory Construction and Retrieval via Evidence-Preserving Multi-Anchor Hypergraph
items.summary: EdgeMem introduces an LLM-free method for agent memory construction and retrieval using an evidence-preserving multi-anchor hypergraph, aiming to avoid cost and data loss from LLM-generated summaries.

items.title: Recovering Temporal and Geographic Signals from Language Model Embeddings
items.summary: This study investigates how language model embeddings encode temporal and geographic real-world information, using a projection-based method for representation analysis and information retrieval.

items.title: LoGIC: Budgeted Context Construction for Node-Level Graph In-Context Learning with Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper introduces LoGIC, a method for budgeted context construction in node-level graph in-context learning using tabular foundation models. It focuses on how labeled rows serve as prompts and addresses the issue of current protocols employing the complete training table as context.

items.title: Memory in Deep Time-Series Models
items.summary: This work examines the concept of "memory" across various deep learning architectural paradigms for time series models, from recurrent networks and transformers to retrieval-augmented predictors and foundation models. It highlights how these systems store and recall information over time.

items.title: Compressed Recurrent Feedback in Tsetlin Machines: A Reproducible Boolean-FSM Study
items.summary: This study explores compressed recurrent feedback in Tsetlin Machines (RTM) as a mechanism for models to retain useful history for sequential inference on small devices. It describes how RTMs provide memory by feeding Boolean clause outputs from one time step as inputs to the next.

items.title: PACE: Perceived-Latency-Aware Cascading Service Routing and Filler Control for QoE-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Dialogue Serving
items.summary: This paper presents PACE, a framework for retrieval-augmented dialogue serving that optimizes for perceived latency to first response while managing quality and cost constraints.

items.title: Tactile Memory with Soft Robot: Robust Object Insertion via Masked Encoding and Soft Wrist
items.summary: This research introduces TaMeSo-bot, a system that integrates a soft robot wrist with tactile memory and retrieval capabilities to improve robust object insertion in contact-rich tasks.

items.title: Show HN: Ambient Context v1.0.0 (Missing context for AI assistants)
items.summary: Ambient Context v1.0.0 is a macOS app that captures screen text into a markdown file, designed to provide missing context for AI assistants. This tool aims to enhance AI systems' ability to access and recall relevant information from the user's display.

items.title: An anti-RAG AI memory in Rust that intentionally forgets and hallucinates
items.summary: Selmem is an AI memory system developed in Rust that deliberately diverges from Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by intentionally incorporating forgetting and hallucination mechanisms.

items.title: Turning Quick Notes into Long-Term AI Memory
items.summary: The article discusses methods for converting quick notes into long-term memory for AI systems.

items.title: When Quantization Breaks Memory: Recurrent-State Write-Back in Low-Precision Temporal Inference
items.summary: This research investigates how quantization impacts memory in recurrent neural networks, specifically focusing on recurrent-state write-back in low-precision temporal inference.

items.title: Continual Graph Memory for Adaptive Recommendation under Intent Drift
items.summary: This paper studies continual graph memory for adaptive recommendation systems that operate under intent drift, using Knowledge Graphs to store and retrieve relational evidence. The memory mechanism helps adapt recommendations based on feedback.

items.title: Shadow Queries for Private Retrieval in Vector Databases
items.summary: This paper proposes "Shadow Queries" to enhance private retrieval in cloud-based vector databases used by large language models (LLMs) for information retrieval systems like RAG.

items.title: KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU
items.summary: KVMem introduces a system for virtualizing million-token agent workspaces on a consumer GPU, designed to manage the persistent memory and accumulated history of LLM agents. This addresses the challenge of agent context exceeding both GPU KV capacity and the model's native context window.

items.title: BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference
items.summary: This paper introduces BeaconKV, a method for compressing the key-value (KV) cache in large reasoning models. It aims to address memory bottlenecks caused by linearly growing KV caches during extended Chain-of-Thought generation.

items.title: CAGE: Coherence-Aware Graph Encoding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces Coherence-Aware Graph Encoding (CAGE), a reranking framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. CAGE models coherence between retrieved chunks to improve the quality of context sets, addressing the issue of individually relevant but collectively incoherent passages.

items.title: NS-ST-GraphRAG: Neuro-Symbolic Spatio-Temporal GraphRAG for Literary Knowledge Processing
items.summary: This paper introduces NS-ST-GraphRAG, a neuro-symbolic spatio-temporal GraphRAG system designed to address the challenges of processing long-form literary narratives for retrieval-augmented generation.

items.title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: A Two-Stage Training Recipe for Soft Context Compression in RAG
items.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage training recipe for soft context compression in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems to address issues of lengthy retrieved context and improve inference efficiency. It focuses on encoding documents into shorter embedding sequences for better RAG performance.

items.title: Linguistic Trajectory Encoding for Efficient Long-Horizon Spatial Memory in Embodied Agents
items.summary: This paper proposes Linguistic Trajectory Encoding as a method for efficient long-horizon spatial memory in embodied agents, allowing them to store and recall state transitions of dynamic objects in natural language over extended periods. It addresses the need for fine-grained motion recall beyond typical video-language embeddings.

items.title: EmbodiedLGR: Integrating Lightweight Graph Representation and Retrieval for Semantic-Spatial Memory in Robotic Agents
items.summary: EmbodiedLGR integrates lightweight graph representation and retrieval to provide semantic-spatial memory for robotic agents, enabling efficient information storage and recall in complex environments.

items.title: Show HN: CellularFlow – Continual-learning LLM using associative memory
items.summary: CellularFlow is presented as a project focused on developing a continual-learning LLM that utilizes an associative memory mechanism for information storage and recall.

items.title: AI coding agents forget the codebase between sessions
items.summary: This item highlights a problem where AI coding agents fail to retain knowledge of the codebase between sessions, pointing to challenges in long-term memory for AI systems.

items.title: Perplexity Details Its GPU Embedding Stack: How Ivy, Tulip and ROSE Serve pplx-embed
items.summary: Perplexity Engineering details its GPU embedding stack, including Ivy, Tulip, and ROSE, explaining how it serves its 'pplx-embed' for efficient retrieval.

items.title: OKF Agent Memory – Git-native persistent memory for AI coding agents
items.summary: A new project called 'OKF Agent Memory' introduces a Git-native persistent memory solution specifically designed for AI coding agents.

items.title: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory
items.summary: The article provides guidance on designing memory lifecycle policies for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to manage and prune long-running AI agent memories.

items.title: Customizing your knowledge base on Amazon Bedrock for large and complex documents using Amazon Textract
items.summary: The article details how to customize an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base for large, complex documents by integrating Amazon Textract for text extraction and enabling efficient querying of processed information.

items.title: How to edit Claude's memory
items.summary: This item discusses how to edit Claude's memory, which allows the AI to use past conversations as context for future prompts and emphasizes the importance of accurate conversational memory.

items.title: Fresh Memory, Stale Plans: Dependency-Scoped Validation for Distributed LLM-Agent Memory
items.summary: This research addresses the issue of "stale-plan execution" in distributed LLM-agent teams, where agents may act on outdated plans despite access to fresh shared facts, proposing a dependency-scoped validation for agent memory.

items.title: GrowPage: On-Demand KV Budgeting for Efficient LLM Reasoning Serving
items.summary: This paper introduces GrowPage, a method for on-demand KV budgeting to optimize the key-value cache and improve the efficiency of LLM reasoning serving, especially for long-output tasks.

items.title: STAIR (STructure Aware Information Retriever): A novel dataset and LLM based retriever for document structure augmentation
items.summary: This item introduces STAIR, a novel LLM-based retriever and dataset for document structure augmentation, enhancing Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) by improving information retrieval.

items.title: RecurTrace: Adaptive Latent Reasoning with Loop-Time Memory
items.summary: This paper introduces RecurTrace, an adaptive latent reasoning method that utilizes 'Loop-Time Memory' to enhance a language model's effective inference depth by managing information across iterative processing blocks.

items.title: Bounded Personas Match Retrieval on Classification but Not Regression for a Frozen Agent
items.summary: This paper examines how personalized language agents utilize retrieval of user interaction history to generate responses, comparing its effectiveness on classification versus regression tasks for a fixed agent. It highlights trade-offs between accuracy and cost for retrieval-based personalization.

items.title: R$^{2}$Adapter: A Routing and Rewriting Adapter for Efficient Hybrid RAG
items.summary: This paper introduces R^2Adapter, a routing and rewriting adapter designed to enhance Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Large Language Models. It aims to improve efficiency and performance for complex relational or multi-hop reasoning queries that vanilla RAG struggles with.

items.title: MemoryLACE: Memory Lifecycle-Aware Consolidation and Evidence Retrieval
items.summary: Introduces MemoryLACE, a system for long-term LLM agents to manage and retrieve information across interactions, addressing limitations of existing textual memory systems.

items.title: SGD-KV: Summarization Guided KV Cache Compression
items.summary: Introduces SGD-KV, a summarization-guided technique for compressing the KV cache in LLMs to address memory bottlenecks during long-context inference.

items.title: Lngram v2: Latent N-Gram Memory with Interpretable Discrete Representations
items.summary: Introduces Lngram v2, an improved latent n-gram memory mechanism for Transformers that uses interpretable discrete representations for efficient lookup and reuse of local patterns.

items.title: Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning
items.summary: Introduces Random Attention, a novel method for KV cache eviction designed to mitigate memory bottlenecks in Large Language Models during extended reasoning tasks.

items.title: When Retrieval Helps: Selective Retrieval for Single-Turn Mental-Health QA
items.summary: This paper investigates the effectiveness of selective retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in single-turn mental-health question answering, finding that its benefits are not uniform due to the complex nature of user queries.

items.title: When Users Don't Ask: Benchmarking Context-Driven Memory Retrieval in Conversational Agents
items.summary: This paper introduces LOCOMO-CONV, a new benchmark to evaluate context-driven memory retrieval in long-horizon conversational agents, addressing the limitations of existing QA-style memory benchmarks.
